build: Remember's crack, release 15: cracked from tape, docs by HOK, +2 trainer by Jack Alien; one file, M.OF MAGIC+2/REM, on a disk named C64.COM. The game starts at $07F9 and runs with no trainer option taken

exclude: BASIC ROM entry the game calls (RAM initialisation, from $0809); the RAM beneath is title data, counted under its own labels
KERNAL ROM entry the game calls (clear screen, from $0806); the RAM beneath is title data
KERNAL ROM interrupt exit the play and title handlers jump to; the RAM beneath is title data
KERNAL ROM entry the game calls (CHROUT); the RAM beneath is title data

comments.text: 6510 data-direction register. The entry code writes $2F to it (LDA #$2F at $07FE, STA $00 at $0800; bits 0-3 and 5 outputs); nothing else in the game touches it.

6510 processor port, the memory banking. The entry sets $37 ($0802) and the restart at $0818 clears bit 0 (AND #$FE), leaving $36 for the whole game: BASIC ROM out so $A000-$BFFF is the game's RAM, I/O and the KERNAL ROM in (CHROUT, the $EA31 interrupt exit, and the ROM bytes $2B9E reads as random numbers). $0002-$0013 are not used by the game's code.
Demonstration recorder and player ($179D): low byte of a pointer to the current input record, copied from $03D4 each time a record is read or written ($17B3, $17F5, $182D, $1927).
High byte of the input-record pointer at $14, copied from $03D5 ($17B8-$192F); the records live at $A543-$A7FF. $0016-$0054 are not used by the game's code.

Low byte of a pointer (with $64) used by four routines: the new-game setup walks it over the map $9000-$9FFF closing every door ($09AE-$09D3); $1695 walks it over the view window at $0400 counting door and passage tiles for the scenery pictures ($16E8-$1734); the block copy $5CC5 reads its parameter block through it and then writes the destination through it; the title interrupt reads the scroller text through it ($5E01-$5E22).

High byte of the pointer at $63: $90-$9F during the map walk, $04 for the view-window scan, the destination's high byte in $5CC5, $80-$83 for the title scroller text. $0065-$009A are not used by the game's code.

Pointer A, low byte (with $9C), the game's main address register, set up afresh by each user: the screen address in the view scroll ($0D44) and view draw ($0F58), the menu window ($1106, $1151, $1320, $1483) and the message window ($28AE-$2941); the glyph copied into a view sprite ($1092: $3000 + 8 x glyph); a map address in OPEN and CLOSE ($1B9D-$1CF9), the passage-tile test ($20CC) and a monster's step ($2566); the picture copy's source ($1515); the string in $2BC7; the block copy's source ($5CC5).
Pointer A, high byte (see $9B). $1483 and $1106 add $D4 to it to reach the colour RAM cell under a screen cell of the menu window, and $1483 takes the $D4 off again afterwards.

Pointer B, low byte (with $9E): mostly the colour-RAM twin of pointer A (screen address + $D400) in the view scroll, view draw, menu and message windows; also the view sprite being filled ($0FEF: $3840 + 64 per slot), the tile glyph the ray tests ($0C41, from $A200/$A300), the picture copy's destination ($1515), a monster's list of preferred headings ($2566, from $4968/$4970) and the block copy's end address ($5CC5).
Pointer B, high byte (see $9D): $D8-$DB when it follows colour RAM, $38-$39 for the view sprites, $30-$37 for a tile glyph, $49 for a heading list.

Ray caster: index (0-120) of the view cell the current ray has reached in the 11 x 11 view arrays $3D45/$3DBE/$3E37. Starts at 60, the centre and the player's own cell ($0B70); +1/-1 when the ray crosses into the tile right/left, +11/-11 down/up ($0BAA-$0C1F); $0C77 records the cell under it. $00BC-$00C4 are not used by the game's code.

KERNAL: matrix code (8 x row + column) of the key held: its scan in $EA31, which band 0 of the play interrupt ends in, writes 64 to $CB and then the key found ($EA8C, $EAC9) and copies $CB here ($EB28, in the emulator's kernal-901227-03.bin). The game reads it: $24 M toggles the music ($0C94); $1D H up, $1C B down, $3C SPACE fire ($0CFF-$0D19); $15 F ends a recording ($17AD); on the title $11 R with CTRL starts one ($5BC1). $00C6-$00CB are not used by the game's code.

KERNAL cursor switch: set to 1 by the entry ($080E) and never read by the game. The KERNAL interrupt skips its cursor blink while it is non-zero ($EA34 LDA $CC / BNE in kernal-901227-03.bin), so the $EA31 exit of the play interrupt never flashes a cursor into the game screen. $00CD-$00E1 are not used by the game's code.

Ray caster: the ray's pixel column 0-7 inside its tile, starting at the player's $3FF0 ($0B5C). Stepping past 7 or below 0 wraps it and moves $F9/$FA and $BB one tile right or left ($0BE8-$0C1F). Indexes the pixel masks $3BE7/$3BEF of the sight test.

Ray caster: the ray's pixel row 0-7 inside its tile, from the player's $4030 ($0B61). Wrapping moves $F9/$FA by $80 (one map row) and $BB by 11 ($0B92-$0BDB); it is the glyph row read by the sight test ($0C4B).

Two uses. Ray caster: low byte of the map address of the tile the ray is in, from the player's $3F70 ($0B66); $0C77 stores it per view cell in $3D45. Message printer $2941: low byte of the string being printed (X on entry, $2941), advanced word by word.
High byte of $F9: the ray's map address ($90-$9F, from $3FB0, stored in $3DBE) or, in $2941, the string's high byte (Y on entry).

Music driver play routine ($C006): low byte of the current voice's track pointer (its list of pattern numbers), loaded from $C4AF + voice ($C062); read at $C07D for the next pattern, $FF looping the track and $FE stopping the tune.
Music driver: high byte of the track pointer, from $C4B2 + voice ($C067).
Music driver: low byte of the current pattern's pointer, from $C4C7 + pattern number ($C09F); the note, duration and instrument bytes are read through it ($C0B1-$C14F).
Music driver: high byte of the pattern pointer, from $C4F0 + pattern number ($C0A4).

Ray caster: index into the step table $3BF7 of the current ray's next step. Set to the ray's pattern start from $3BCB ($0B7C), advanced per step, and reset to that start every 7 steps ($0C38), so a ray repeats its 7-step pattern.

KERNAL: the SHIFT/Commodore/CTRL flags of its keyboard scan, which ORs in 1 for either SHIFT, 2 for the Commodore key and 4 for CTRL (key table $EB81, $EAC1 in kernal-901227-03.bin); the game only reads it. In play ($0CEA) 1 makes the horizontal input +1, right, and 2 makes it -1, left, as the controls screen documents; on the title 4 (CTRL alone) with R starts a recording ($5BBA-$5BCC). $028E-$02A5 are not used by the game.

KERNAL: its video-standard flag, set at reset from the raster interrupt flag ($FF63-$FF68 in kernal-901227-03.bin; its timer setup at $FDDD treats non-zero as PAL); 1 in the PAL snapshots. The game only reads it: when it is 0, an NTSC machine at 60 frames a second, $1949 skips every sixth music tick ($03DB) and the title scroller every second step ($5DAC, $03DA). $02A7-$02E5 are not used by the game.

KERNAL IRQ vector, low byte (with $0315): the KERNAL's interrupt entry jumps through it. The game sets it to the play interrupt $2653 ($2627), to the title interrupt $5D08 ($5B90), and back to the KERNAL's $EA31 while it rebuilds a screen ($5B27, $5C19).
KERNAL IRQ vector, high byte: $26, $5D or $EA. $0316-$0354 are not used by the game (the BRK and NMI vectors at $0316-$0319 keep the KERNAL's values).

Ray caster ($0B25): the ray being cast, 0-27, one of 28 directions; +1 per call, wrapping at 28, and indexing $3BCB for its step pattern. A turn step casts six rays ($08CC); $0B05 casts 30 at once, starting it at $1B so the first is ray 0. 0 at game start ($0929).
Ray caster: steps the current ray has taken. The ray ends at 56 ($38) steps or at the first opaque pixel ($0C69-$0C71); $0C77 records no cell once it is 56.
Ray caster: position 0-6 in the ray's 7-step pattern; at 7 it returns to 0 and $FF goes back to the pattern's start ($0C26-$0C3B).

Random numbers ($2B9E): offset into the KERNAL ROM at $E000, +1 per number. With $0384 it is the generator's whole state: a recording stores the pair at $A540/$A541 ($5BD3) and the demonstration loads it back ($5DF2), so the replay meets the same luck.

Random numbers ($2B9E): offset into the KERNAL ROM at $E800, -3 per number. The number is ROM[$F000 + ROM[$E000 + $0383]] EOR ROM[$E800 + $0384]; with $01 = $36 the CPU reads the ROM, not the title data in the RAM beneath.
Random numbers: $2B9E keeps the caller's X here ($2B9E) and restores it on exit ($2BC0).
Random numbers: $2B9E keeps the caller's Y here ($2BA1) and restores it on exit ($2BC3).

Input ($0CC6): 1 while fire on joystick port 2 or SPACE ($0D15) is held, else 0. The demonstration writes recorded fire into it ($18AE). Read by the menu ($133A, $137E), the move loop ($0904), the title and every wait for fire.

Input: horizontal direction, $FF left, 0, 1 right, from joystick port 2 ($0CD5-$0CE4), then SHIFT (1) and the Commodore key ($FF) override it ($0CEA). The move adds it to the player's $3FF0 ($0D60); a wall collision flips its sign ($0F95); in a menu it moves the cursor one item ($13A1).

Input: vertical direction, $FF up, 0, 1 down, from joystick port 2, then H ($FF) and B (1) override it ($0CFF). The move adds it to the player's $4030 ($0D7E); flipped by a wall collision; in a menu it moves the cursor a row ($13E6); down (B) on the controls screen shows the instructions ($5C82).

Scratch byte shared by many routines: the game-over wait's low count ($0882-$0893); a row counter in the view scroll ($0E79-$0F1B); the saved index in the view draw ($0F6F); the sprite enable bit being placed by the multiplexer ($0FF4-$10CF); the column distance in the heading finder ($219B); the monster being stepped ($225F-$22F5); damage in a monster's attack ($2481-$24D0) and the player's ($2B08-$2B49); the alternative tried in a monster's step ($2569-$2614).

Set to 1 when the player moves into another tile ($0DA0, $0DF6, $0E51, $0EC3) and by the rebuild $0B05. The next ray ($0B34) clears it, restarts the sweep count $039F and empties the view arrays ($0F45), whose cells are relative to the tile the player was in.
Turn step ($08CC): counts 0-5 while the step casts one ray ($0B25) and ticks every monster ($2205) six times, before the clock, spell upkeep, player's move and sprites.

Sprite-to-background collisions of the top and menu bands: band 2 of the play interrupt ORs $D01F into it every frame ($27BB; band 0 reads $D01F only to clear it). Bit 0 means the player's dot, sprite 0, touched a wall pixel: the move then reverses the direction for one step ($0AD3, $0F95), and fire cannot end the move while it is set ($091C).

Scratch byte: the sprite enable mask the multiplexer builds ($1001-$10FC, then $3A10); the game-over wait's middle count ($0885, $0898); names printed so far in INVENTORY ($1A96-$1ADD); the row distance in the heading finder ($21BE-$21FE, $212D); cleared by a monster's step ($256F).

Scratch byte: the game-over wait's top count, which returns to the title at 10 ($089D-$08A5); low byte of player - $CD - object map address in the multiplexer ($1023-$1061); the item in INVENTORY ($1AAD); the larger distance in the heading finder ($211F-$2177); low byte of the 'from' address given to it ($2384, $23B2, $23D8).

Scratch byte: high byte of the multiplexer's map-address difference, made into a row offset ($102B-$1073); names printed so far in LOOK IN ($2053-$2095); the smaller distance in the heading finder ($2133-$217B); high byte of the 'from' address given to it ($238A, $23B8, $23DE).
Scratch byte: sprite register offset (2 x slot) of the next multiplexed sprite ($0FF9-$10D5); low byte of the 'to' map address given to the heading finder ($2390, $23BE, $23E4; read at $21A3, $21D9).

Scratch byte: the object's column offset ($1046) and then the glyph row count of the sprite copy ($10B6-$10C8) in the multiplexer; in the heading finder the high byte of the 'to' address made into a row ($2396-$21E8), then the 4-bit case that indexes the heading table $4947 ($2116-$2194).

Scratch byte: the sprite slot 0-6 the multiplexer is filling, which stops at 7 ($0FFC-$10ED); in the heading finder the ratio of the larger to the smaller distance ($215F-$2185, $20 when the smaller is 0), 2 or more meaning mostly straight.

Sprite multiplexer ($0FEF): the object (1-63) to consider first. Each call gives sprites 1-7 to the first seven objects in view ($3EB0) from here, wrapping 63 to 1, and saves where it stopped ($1102), so more than seven take turns. 1 at game start ($09E7).
Menu window: low byte (with $0396) of the screen address where $1151 prints the next line; set to the window's corner $03C5 by $1106 and advanced by the item width $03BE per line ($1186).
Menu window: high byte of the next line's screen address ($0395), from $03C6.

Menu window: lines printed so far, 0 after $1106 clears the window. $1151 stores each line's value at $41C8 + this count and prints nothing once it equals the capacity $03BF; handlers test it for an empty list ($19B9, $1B33).
Menu cursor: the item it was on before the last move ($1393), put back if the move lands on an empty cell ($143F).
Menu cursor: index of the highlighted item, 0 = the first line ($132C); moved by the stick ($13A8-$1434); on fire $147C returns $41C8 + this.
Turn steps per pixel the player moves: 2 for WALK ($08B0), 1 for RUN ($08B9); reloads the countdown $039C. The menu never offers WALK, so in practice it is 1.
PICK UP ($195C): the item 1-32 being checked; those on the player's tile are listed with their pictures.
Countdown to the player's next pixel of movement: $0ABF decrements it every turn step and moves the player at 0, reloading it from $039A. 1 at game start ($09E4). $039D-$039E are not used.

Rays cast in the current sweep of the view, 1-29. At 29 ($0B4A) the sweep is drawn into the view window ($0F58), the objects in view are found again ($0FAA) and the view arrays are emptied for the next sweep ($0F45). Cleared with $038B.
Frame counter: +1 per frame in band 2 of the play interrupt ($27B8). The move loop waits for it to change ($0914, $0ACA, $0AF1), so the player moves at most one pixel a frame.
Frame counter value at the player's last pixel of movement ($0AFC); $0ACA waits for $03A0 to differ from it.

PICK UP: the load total. Starts at the chosen item's weight ($4A01, $19EF); $2883 adds everything the player carries, with the contents of carried containers, and everything inside the chosen item. 70 or more ($1A03) refuses it with the message at $46B2.
Message window: column 0-26 of the bottom line where the next word goes; 0 after a scroll ($293D) or a clear ($28D9).
Message printer ($2941): first the column the next word would end at, to decide whether to scroll first ($2976), then the column being written ($29A1).
Message printer: index of the next byte of the current word in the string at $F9/$FA ($295E-$29BE).

Message printer: colour of the characters it writes ($29AD). A byte below $20 in a string sets it to that byte's low nibble ($29E3), so the $10 before every verb prints the verb in black. 1, white, at game start ($09ED).

The object an action is about: the item or creature chosen in a submenu (PICK UP, PUT DOWN, WEAR, TAKE OFF, PUT IN, TAKE OUT, LOOK IN, ATTACK, EXAMINE, DRINK, a spell's target), the spell chosen in CAST ($2E4D), the monster attacking ($2404); elsewhere a loop's saved index ($16B3, $177F).

A second object or an amount: the container chosen in PUT IN ($1EAC), each item found in LOOK IN ($2065), the weapon in the right hand for ATTACK, 0 bare-handed ($2A95), the weapon an attacking monster carries ($2422-$245A), the damage passed to the spell hit $3AC7 ($3AC7).
Menu builder ($128F): items 1-32 on the player's tile; PICK UP is offered when non-zero ($11B7).
Menu builder: carried items that can be worn ($4A81) and are not worn ($4AC1 = 0); WEAR when non-zero.
Menu builder: carried containers ($4A41); TAKE OUT and LOOK IN when non-zero, PUT IN too if a hand is full.
Menu builder: carried items being worn ($4AC1 = 2); TAKE OFF when non-zero.
Menu builder: hands holding something, 0-2 ($4C01, $4C02 not $FF); PUT DOWN and SWAP when non-zero.
Menu builder: creatures $21-$3F on the player's tile, dead ones too ($1305-$131D); ATTACK when non-zero.

Turn steps the chosen verb still takes: $4C27 + option on each choice ($0833); the step loop at $08CC counts it down ($090E) and returns to the menu at 0. For WALK and RUN it is 0 and the loop runs until fire.
Message window: low byte of its top-left screen address, $5C ($09FC): $045C, row 2 column 12.
Message window: high byte of the top-left address, $04 ($0A01).
Message window: width in characters, 27 ($0A06).
Message window: height in rows, 8 ($0A0B); a scroll moves rows 1-7 up one.
Message window: low byte of the bottom line's address, $74 ($0A10): $0574, row 9 column 12, where text is written before the window scrolls.
Message window: high byte of the bottom line's address, $05 ($0A15). $03B6 is not used.
Play interrupt: which band the next interrupt is: 0 at raster $28 (top band), 1 at $8E (menu band), 2 at $B6 (picture band); set to 0 when the interrupt is installed ($2649). $03B8 is not used.

Monster step ($2566): 1 when the heading taken is open only through a door (passable in the monster's table but not in $A100, $25C6); the monster then opens the door ($1BBF) and marks it to be closed behind it ($4FE2).
Monster step: the monster's index kept across the door calls ($25E5-$260D).
Status line ($2BDE): units left to draw while it draws the M bar (mind $4F46 x 2) and the B bar (body $4EC5 + 1, x 2): a full cell, glyph $29, per 8 units, then glyph $21 + the rest.
Clock: counts turn steps down from 8; at 0 $2C50 adds a second to the clock on the top line ($0420-$0427). 4 at game start ($09F5).
Menu builder: carried items that can be drunk ($4B41); DRINK when non-zero.
Menu window: characters per item, 10 for the main menu ($3A79) and 20 for the spell menu ($3A93); lines advance by it, so items fill each 40-column row left to right.
Menu window: items it holds, 16 or 8: $1106 clears that many, $1151 stops printing there, the cursor cannot pass it.
Menu window: items per screen row, 4 or 2: the cursor's step for up and down ($1407, $1431).
Menu window: first item of the bottom row, 12 or 6: down is refused from there ($13F0).
Menu window: first item of the second row, 4 or 2: up is refused before it ($141A).
Spell upkeep ($3A40): turn steps counted to 100 while a lasting spell ($57D2) is in force; by $57D9 the only lasting spell is MAGICAL SHIELD. Cleared by UNCAST ($2F3B).

Spell upkeep: hundreds of turn steps; when it reaches the spell's interval ($57D9 + spell, 1 for MAGICAL SHIELD) the player loses a point of mind ($3A66) and it restarts, so the shield costs one mind per 100 turn steps; with no mind left the spell ends ($2F22).
Menu window: low byte of its top-left screen address, $E0 ($09D7): $05E0, row 12 column 0.
Menu window: high byte of the top-left address, $05 ($09DC).

0 while the game runs. 1 when the player dies ($24E7) or a demonstration or recording ends ($17C5-$191D); $7B when the amulet is put down on the pedestal's tile ($1B96). The main loop ($0827, $084C) and the menu ($1332) stop on it; $7B selects the ending text and tune 2.
Counts turn steps to 50 ($3B87); then creatures $22, $23, $2A, $2B, $2E, $33 and $35 get new random destinations ($4CAE/$4CCD).
View rebuild ($0B05): counts the 30 rays it casts at once (every direction and two more).
Picture strip ($1515): the object being shown ($155E), then its picture number from $582B ($15C5).
Picture strip: the slot 0-11 the picture goes in ($1561).
Picture strip: the object's size flag passed in A (its $586F): 0 one slot, four character rows; non-zero two slots, eight rows ($1515).
Picture strip: character rows to copy, 4 or 8 ($1518-$1524).
Menu cursor: blink timer 0-29; the highlighted item is coloured 0 (black) at 0 and 1 (white) at 20 ($1344-$1370).

Set to 1 for one noise burst on voice 1, a footstep: by the player every third pixel moved ($0D5D) and by a monster in view with a $59DC flag every third step ($2254). Band 1 of the interrupt plays it and clears it, when the music is off ($2778).
Counts the player's moving steps down from 3; at 0 a footstep ($03CF). 1 at game start ($09EA).
1 while the music plays: band 1 of the interrupt calls $1949 every frame ($2773); 0 lets the footstep noises through. Set by $2627 and at the end of a game ($0866), toggled by M ($0CA4).
M key debounce: 1 while M is held ($0CA1), so a press toggles the music once.

Input source: 0 play; 1 recording, started by CTRL+R on the title ($5BCE): every input goes into the demonstration buffer; 2 the demonstration, started when the title scroller has run ($5BE9): input comes from the buffer ($179D).
Demonstration buffer: low byte of the current record's address (with $03D5), $42 at game start ($0A7E); it is advanced before use, so the first record is $A543.
Demonstration buffer: high byte, $A5 at game start; reaching $A8 ends a recording or the demonstration ($17E6, $1867, $1912).
Demonstration: the current record's input: bit 0 right, 1 left, 2 down, 3 up, $F fire, $E end. A record is this code in the high nibble and a repeat count 0-15 in the low nibble.
Demonstration: plays left of the current record; $FF means read the next one ($189B, $193A).
Set when a demonstration ends, by fire, its end record or the buffer's end: the game then goes straight back to the title ($0876) without the game-over wait.
Title: set to 2 by the title interrupt when the scroller has run once ($5DEF); the title loop then starts the demonstration ($5BE4).
Title scroller on NTSC ($02A6 = 0): counts down from 2 and the step that reaches 0 is skipped ($5DB1), so every second step is dropped. 1 at the entry ($0815).

Music on NTSC: counts down from 6 and the tick that reaches 0 is skipped ($194E), keeping PAL tempo at 60 frames a second. $03DC-$03FF are left over from the crack's decruncher (same bytes as at the entry) and not used.
Screen row 0, columns 13-20: the M (mind) bar, 8 cells drawn by $2BDE from the player's mind $4F46 (glyphs $21-$29).
Screen row 0, columns 23-30: the B (body) bar, 8 cells drawn by $2BDE from the player's body strength $4EC5.
Clock on the status line, tens of hours: '0'-'9', back to '0' after 99 hours ($2CBF-$2CD0).
Clock: units of hours ($2CAF-$2CC4).
Clock: tens of minutes, '0'-'5' ($2C9A-$2CAC).
Clock: units of minutes ($2C85-$2C97).
Clock: tens of seconds, '0'-'5' ($2C70-$2C82).
Clock: units of seconds, +1 every 8 turn steps ($2C5B, $03BC).
The view window's centre cell, row 5 column 5: the player's tile. When it holds a door ($F0-$FF) the menu offers OPEN (bit 0 clear) or CLOSE (bit 0 set) ($11E5).
Screen row 24: the title's scrolling line; the title interrupt writes 40 characters of the story text here with colour 7 ($5E15).

Sprite pointers of the screen at $0400, $07F8-$07FF: $E0-$E7 ($0A6B), so band 0's sprites take their shapes from $3800-$39FF; sprite 0 is set again at $0D40. Until the game sets them, $07F9-$07FF hold the entry code.

Entry: the game's first instruction, where the crack's trainer jumps (JMP $07F9). At load these seven bytes are 78 D8 A2 FF 9A A9 2F: SEI, CLD, LDX #$FF, TXS (an empty stack), LDA #$2F, followed by the STA $00 at $0800. They lie in the sprite-pointer bytes of the top band's screen ($0400), and new_game overwrites them with the pointers $E0-$E7 ($0A66 loop), so every snapshot taken in play shows E1-E7 here (typed as bytes for that reason). Runs once per power-on: the reset and RESTORE vectors of the CBM80 block at $8000 point at restart ($0818), not here.

Two bytes that held 85 00 at load: the entry's STA $00, which puts the $2F loaded at $07FE into the 6510's data direction register. BASIC's RAM initialisation, called at $0809, then stores a zero at the bottom of BASIC memory (STA ($2B),Y at $E419 in the ROM, $2B/$2C from MEMBOT), which replaces the $85: entry-07f9.vsf has 85 here, every later snapshot 00. The instruction has run by then and nothing executes these bytes again.

Entry, continued: $01 = $37 (BASIC, I/O and KERNAL visible), JSR $E544 (KERNAL: clear the screen), JSR $E3BF (BASIC: initialise its RAM and zero page), $CC = 1 (the KERNAL interrupt, which the play interrupt ends in, then never flashes a cursor: $EA34 skips the blink while $CC is non-zero), and $03DB = $03DA = 1, the NTSC frame-skip counters of the play music tick ($1949, reloaded with 6) and of the title interrupt ($5DB1, reloaded with 2); both count only when $02A6 = 0, an NTSC machine. Set once per power-on. Falls into restart.

Restart: where the entry falls through, where the game-over wait jumps, and the target of both CBM80 vectors ($8000 cold, $8002 warm), so a reset or RESTORE lands here too (the KERNAL's $FCE2 and $FE47 test for CBM80 and JMP through them). Clears bit 0 of $01 ($37 becomes $36: BASIC ROM out, so the game's data under it at $A000-$BFFF reads as RAM), runs the title, story scroller, demonstration and controls screen (JSR $5B27: it returns when a game is to start, after the controls screen; with $03D3 = 2 when the scroller has run and the demonstration is to be played by the main loop; or with $03D3 = 1, the input recorder, after CTRL+R on the title), sets up a new game (JSR $0924) and falls into main_loop. The stack pointer is not reset here.

Main loop, once per menu choice: redraws the M(ind) and B(ody) bars (JSR $2BDE); if the game is over ($03C7 non-zero) goes to game_over; otherwise the menu (JSR $11A2) returns the chosen verb number in A (0 WALK .. 17 UNCAST). $4C27+verb, the number of world passes the action lasts, goes to $03AF (0 for WALK and RUN, which last until fire); $4C3A+verb (twice the verb) indexes the handler table at $4C03, and the handler's address is written into the operand of the JSR at $0846 ($0847/$0848), which then calls it: a self-modifying dispatch. The operand in the snapshot is $08B9, RUN, the last verb chosen.

Low byte of the dispatch JSR's operand (the instruction at $0846), rewritten at $083D with the low byte of the chosen verb's handler from $4C03,x. $46 at load, when the instruction reads JSR $0846, a call to itself that the main loop never lets run; $B9 in the snapshot (RUN, $08B9).
High byte of the dispatch JSR's operand, rewritten at $0843 from $4C04,x, the handler table's high bytes. $08 at load and in the snapshot, where RUN ($08B9) was the last verb chosen.
After the verb's handler returns: runs the world for the action's time (JSR $08CC, run_world), then goes round main_loop again while the game is not over ($03C7 = 0).

Game over ($03C7 non-zero). $7B is the win, set at $1B96 when the amulet (object $15) is put down while the player stands on the pedestal's map cell $9677: the ending at $5A5C ('WITH A SUDDEN FLASH OF CRIMSEN LIGHT THELRIC APPEARS...') is printed in the message window and tune 2 starts (JSR $C000, A = 2; HVSC's third tune, 'Game beaten'). Any other value, 1 for a death ($24E7, body strength below zero) or for a game stopped by the demonstration or the input recorder, starts tune 1 (HVSC's 'Game Over (You're dead)'). Both set $03D1 = 1 so the interrupt plays it.

Waits before going back to the title. If the demonstration ended the game ($03D8 set at $1892, $18CA or $1920: fire pressed during it, its end code, or the end of its buffer) it restarts at once. Otherwise it waits 256 rounds of the delay routine (JSR $0F35, A = $FF: about 1.7 s on PAL), clears a 24-bit count ($038A/$038E/$038F) and polls the stick and keys (JSR $179D) until fire, when it waits for the release (JSR $5E29) and restarts, or until the count reaches $0A0000, 655,360 polls (about 135 cycles each: roughly a minute and a half on PAL by the cycle count, not measured), when it restarts anyway.

WALK handler, verb 0: $039A = 2, so the player's movement tick ($0ABF) runs on every second world pass instead of every pass, and clears the picture strip (JSR $149E); unlike RUN it prints nothing. Nothing in this build offers it: the main menu builder ($11B4-$1288) adds verbs 1-17 only, each with an immediate string pointer, and no code loads WALK's string at $4130 (byte scan of the image). Only the handler table's entry 0 ($4C03) points here.

RUN handler, verb 1: $039A = 1, so the movement tick ($0ABF) runs on every world pass; clears the picture strip (JSR $149E) and prints 'RUN' ($4136, its first byte $10 sets text colour 0) and then '.' and a new line (JSR $29F1) in the message window. Its time in $4C27 is 0, so run_world keeps the player moving until fire is pressed.

Runs the world after a verb, one pass per round: six times one ray of the line-of-sight view (JSR $0B25) followed by the creatures' timers and actions (JSR $2205; $038C counts the six); $3B87 (every 50th pass, new random map destinations for seven creatures); the M and B bars ($2BDE); an immediate return if the game is over; the game clock ($2C50: one second per 8 passes, so the clock counts passes and stands still in the menu); the active spell's mind drain ($3A40); only while WALK or RUN runs ($03AF = 0) the player's movement tick ($0ABF) and the picture strip ($1695); the sprites of the visible objects and creatures ($0FEF); and $20BC, which moves any creature, then the player, standing on map cell $B1, $A3 or $B2 by 32 map cells. Then, if fire is down ($0387), it waits for the next frame and returns to the menu unless the player's sprite is touching a wall (bit 0 of $038D), which keeps it going; otherwise WALK and RUN go round until fire, and any other verb until $03AF, its time in passes, has counted down to 0. Only the movement tick polls the input in this loop, so only WALK and RUN can see fire here: a timed verb always runs its full count (live, INVENTORY: 12 passes with fire held and without).

New game, part 1 (called from restart): zeroes the game-over flag $03C7, the ray index $0380 and ray count $039F, $03D8 (demonstration ended), the new-cell flag $038B, the spell-drain counters $03C3/$03C4, the top band's sprite expand, priority and multicolour images $3A11-$3A14 and the bottom band's sprite enable $3A30. Then, for y = 0-63 (0 the player, 1-32 objects, 33-63 creatures): map address back to the starting one ($3EF0/$3F30 into $3F70/$3FB0), in-cell pixel 4,4 ($3FF0/$4030, the cell's middle), $40B0 = $FF (no movement direction), $4AC1 = 0 (neither worn nor in a container), the action timer $4BC1 = 0, body strength $4EC5 = its starting value $4E85, mind $4F46 = the maximum $4F05 (only entry 0's is shown, as the M bar), the footstep counter $5A1C = 1, and $4CEC,y = $4D0B,y = 0. Those two are creature-only tables (read with y = $21-$3F: the pursuit flags set at $237D/$2377 when a creature sees the player), so the 64-byte loops clear $4CEC-$4D4A: their own entries ($4D0D-$4D4A) and also $4CEE-$4D0C, every creature's wander-destination high byte ($4CCD,y, set by $3B87), and $4CEC-$4CED, the destination low bytes ($4CAE,y) of creatures $3E and $3F. All of that loads as zero, so only a restarted game notices. Then $4ADA = 1 (object $19, a scroll, starts in a container: its address is $0007, the backpack), no picture slot holds a bottom-band sprite ($59BD-$59C8 = $FF), no spell is active ($57D2 = $FF), the shield's defence bonus is off ($57D3 = 0), and both hands are empty ($4C02 left, $4C01 right = $FF).

New game, part 2: closes every door in the dungeon map. Walks $9000-$9FFF through the pointer $63/$64 and clears bit 0 of every byte from $F0 to $FF that has it set; those characters are the door cells, and OPEN ($1BBF) sets bit 0 to open one. At load every door is already closed, so this matters for the second and later games.

New game, part 3: the menu's first screen cell $03C5/$03C6 = $05E0 (row 12, column 0), the main menu's layout values $03BE-$03C2 (JSR $3A79), the movement tick due on the first pass ($039C = 1), the entity-sprite scan starting at entry 1 ($0394 = 1), the player's footstep counter $03D0 = 1, text colour white ($03A6 = 1), the view cells cleared (JSR $0F45), the clock's first second after 4 passes ($03BC = 4; $2C50 reloads 8), and the message window: top left $03B0/$03B1 = $045C (row 2, column 12), 27 columns ($03B2), 8 rows ($03B3), printing on its bottom row at $03B4/$03B5 = $0574 (row 9). The LDA #$08 at $09F8 is dead: LDA #$5C replaces it at once.

New game, part 4, the play screen: multicolour characters on ($D016 bit 4), $D018 = $1C (screen $0400, characters $3000 in VIC bank 0), border blue ($D020 = 6), background yellow ($D021 = 7), character multicolours dark grey and grey ($D022 = $0B, $D023 = $0C). Prints the frame through CHROUT (JSR $2BC7 with the string at $50FA: clear screen, the top line with the M and B labels, the bars and the clock's digits, the window borders), then CHROUT $08, which sets bit 7 of $0291 so the KERNAL's scan ($EB54) no longer flips the character set on SHIFT+Commodore, both being movement keys. Clears the top band's sprite shapes $3800-$39FF, draws the player's dot into sprite 0's (rows 0-3 of $3800: $60 $F0 $F0 $60, a 4 x 4 dot in its top left corner), points sprites 0-7 at $E0-$E7 ($07F8-$07FF, shapes $3800-$39FF), marks the bottom band's eight sprites free ($59C9-$59D0 = $FF) and points them all at $94 ($ABF8-$ABFF, the shape at $A500, which spells DEAD).

New game, part 5: the input recorder and demonstration player's state, pointer $03D4/$03D5 = $A542 (its entries are read and written from $A543 on), current input code $03D6 = 7 (a code no stick position makes, so the first input starts a new entry) and repeat count $03D7 = $FF; tune 0 starts (JSR $C000, A = 0; by HVSC's order its 'Main Theme'); the player's sprite (JSR $0D1F); the first view (JSR $0B05); the play raster interrupt (JSR $2627: $0314 = $2653, music on); the message window cleared (JSR $28AE) and Thelric's parting words printed ($46D6, 'AS YOU LEAVE THELRIC SAYS...IF YOU DO NOT BRING ME THE AMULET OF IMMORTALITY...'), then the empty string at $476E (its first byte is the terminator) and a scroll of the window (JSR $28DD); colour RAM $DA58-$DBFE from $A858-$A9FE (JSR $5CC5 with the six-byte descriptor at $57DD: source, end, destination), the bottom rows' colours; and an empty picture strip (JSR $149E).

The player's movement tick, called on every world pass while WALK or RUN runs. Counts $039C down and acts only when it reaches 0, reloading it from $039A (1 for RUN: every pass; 2 for WALK: every other pass). Waits until the frame counter $03A0 has moved on from the frame of the previous tick ($03A1); then, with interrupts off, if the player's sprite touched the background graphics since then (bit 0 of $038D, where band 2 of the interrupt collects $D01F) clears the flag and reverses the step direction (JSR $0F95), else reads the stick and keys (JSR $179D). Moves the player one pixel (JSR $0D44), clears $038D, waits for the next frame, notes it in $03A1 and clears $038D again, so the next tick judges only frames drawn with the new position. Walls are found by the VIC's sprite-background collision, not by reading the map.

Rebuilds the whole view at once: at the start of a game and after PICK UP, PUT DOWN, OPEN and CLOSE ($1A2C, $1B99, $1BBB, $1CFC), when doors or objects have changed. Sets the ray index $0380 to 27 so the next ray is ray 0, sets $038B so the sweep restarts, and casts 30 rays (JSR $0B25, $03C9 counting); the 29th draws the completed view and finds what is visible. Then places the sprites of the visible objects and creatures (JSR $0FEF).

Casts one ray of the line-of-sight view. The ray index $0380 steps through 0-27, 28 directions clockwise from straight up. After the player has entered a new cell ($038B set) the sweep restarts: $039F = 0 and the view cells are cleared (JSR $0F45). $039F counts rays; on the 29th the view gathered so far is drawn (JSR $0F58), the visible entities found (JSR $0FAA) and the cells cleared for the next sweep. The ray starts at the player's exact pixel (in-cell x/y from $3FF0/$4030 into $F7/$F8, map address $3F70/$3FB0 into $F9/$FA, view index $BB = 60, the centre of the 11 x 11 window), records the player's cell (JSR $0C77), then takes up to 56 one-pixel steps ($0381) repeating the ray's seven-step pattern at $3BF7 + $3BCB[ray] (0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, $FF pause; $0382 is the position in it). A step into another cell moves the map address by 1 or $80 (the map is 128 cells wide) and the view index by 1 or 11, and records that cell. After each step the pixel is tested on the cell's character glyph ($A200/$A300 point into the character set at $3000, $3BEF holds the pixel-pair masks): a pair of value %10, or %11 in a character whose colour ($A400) is $0F (every closed door, $F0-$FE even, has it), stops the ray. No pattern moves more than 5 pixels per axis in 7 steps, so a ray reaches at most 5 cells out and stays inside the window.

Records the cell a ray has reached, unless the ray's step count $0381 has reached 56 ($38): the map byte there (a character code) into $3E37[$BB] and its map address into $3D45[$BB] (low) and $3DBE[$BB] (high), $BB being the cell's index in the 11 x 11 view. Returns with Y = 0.

Reads the player's input, with the M key first (called only from $179D). M ($C5 = $24, the KERNAL's current key) toggles the music flag $03D1 once per press ($03D2 remembers that M is down until another key or none is seen). Switching off stops the tune: JSR $C003 asks the driver to stop and JSR $C006 runs it once, which silences the three voices; switching on restarts tune 0 (JSR $C000, A = 0). The play interrupt plays the music while $03D1 is set and the footstep noise ($03CF) only while it is clear. Falls into input_read.

Reads joystick port 2 ($DC00, active low: bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire) into $0389 (y: -1 up, +1 down), $0388 (x: -1 left, +1 right) and $0387 (fire: 1 pressed), then lets the keyboard override, from the KERNAL's scan: $028D = 1 (SHIFT alone) sets x = +1 and $028D = 2 (the Commodore key alone) x = -1; $C5 = $1D (H) sets y = -1, $1C (B) y = +1 and $3C (SPACE) fire = 1. Only one of H, B and SPACE can count at a time, since $C5 holds a single key. B being 'down' is what the controls screen ($5C82) tests for its instructions.

Shows the player as sprite 0 of the top band (called once, from new_game): bit 0 of the sprite-enable image $3A10 set, X = $3E + in-cell x ($3FF0) into $3A00, Y = $58 + in-cell y ($4030) into $3A01, which puts the dot in the middle of the view's centre cell for in-cell 4,4; colour 7, yellow, into $3A15, and the pointer $E0 (the dot at $3800) into $07F8. The interrupt copies $3A00-$3A1C to the VIC in band 0.

Moves the player one pixel by the direction in $0388/$0389 (diagonals too). While moving, every third step ($03D0 counts 3) sets $03CF, the footstep sound the interrupt plays when the music is off. Adds x to the in-cell x $3FF0: reaching 8 or -1 means the next cell to the right or left (player_cross_right, player_cross_left); sprite 0's X image $3A00 = $3E + in-cell x. Then the same for y and $4030 (player_cross_down, player_cross_up), sprite 0's Y image $3A01 = $58 + in-cell y. The dot therefore stays in the view's centre cell while the map scrolls under it.

The player has stepped into the cell to the right: $038B = 1 (restart the view sweep), map address ($3F70/$3FB0) + 1, in-cell x = 0, and the 11 x 11 view window (columns 0-10 of rows 0-10, screen from $0400 through $9B/$9C and colour RAM from $D800 through $9D/$9E) scrolled one cell left; column 10 gets the unseen character $7F in its colour ($A47F). Back into player_step at $0D75.

The player has stepped into the cell to the left: $038B = 1, map address - 1 (borrowing into $3FB0), in-cell x = 7, and the view window scrolled one cell right (each row's columns 9 down to 0 moved up by one); column 0 gets the unseen character $7F. Back into player_step at $0D75.

The player has stepped into the cell below: $038B = 1, map address + $80 (one map row, 128 cells), in-cell y = 0, and the view window scrolled up one row: rows 1-10 copied to rows 0-9 through the offset tables $3D00 (source column + 40) and $3CBB (destination column), ten rows counted in $038A; row 10 gets the unseen character $7F. Back into player_step at $0D96.

The player has stepped into the cell above: $038B = 1, map address - $80, in-cell y = 7, and the view window scrolled down one row: rows 9 up to 0 copied one row lower, starting at row 9 ($0568/$D968) and counting $038A from 9 down; row 0 gets the unseen character $7F. Back into player_step at $0D96.

Busy-wait delay of A + 1 rounds, each 5 x 256 turns of a DEX loop: 6,438 cycles a round, about 6.5 ms on PAL plus whatever the interrupts take. Called with A = 5 by the menu and the title's fire waits, 1 in the menu cursor's blink, $1E after a menu move and $FF (about 1.7 s) before the game-over wait. Returns with A = $FF, X = 0, Y = 0.
Marks all 121 cells of the view as unseen: $7F into the cell characters $3E37 and into the map addresses $3D45/$3DBE, giving the address $7F7F, which no entity ever has.

Draws the view the rays have gathered: for each of the 121 cells, rows 0-10 and columns 0-10 of the screen at $0400 (row stride 40) get the character from $3E37 and colour RAM gets that character's colour from $A400; $038A keeps the cell index while X is borrowed for the colour lookup.
Reverses each non-zero part of the step direction, $0388 and $0389 (EOR #$FE turns +1 into -1 and -1 into +1), so the next step takes the player back out of the wall his sprite has touched.

Finds what the player can see, after each full sweep: clears $3EB0 (seen) and $5041 (distance) for entries 1-63, then for every one of the 121 view cells and every entry whose map address ($3F70/$3FB0) equals the cell's ($3D45/$3DBE) sets $3EB0 = 1, $5041 = the cell's distance from the centre ($5081: 8 x the distance in cells, rounded, and 1 for the player's own cell) and $4C4F/$4C8F = the player's map address, the place where that entity last saw him (read back at $238D). Carried objects (address $00xx) never match a cell.

Shows up to seven of the visible objects and creatures as sprites 1-7 of the top band (continues to $1105). The scan starts at entry $0394 and goes round 1-63, so when more than seven are visible each gets its turn. For each entry with $3EB0 set: its sprite's enable bit ($038A, shifted each time) is ORed into $038E, which starts with the player's bit and ends in $3A10; its X ($3A02+2n) = 59 + 8 dx + in-cell x and Y ($3A03+2n) = 85 + 8 dy + in-cell y, with dx, dy its cell offset from the player worked out from the two map addresses (constants $CD, 16 and the 128-cell row); its colour ($3A16+n) = $A400 of its figure character ($4070); and the figure's eight glyph bytes (from $3000 + 8 x character) are copied into the sprite's shape at $3840 + $40 n. Stops after seven or when the scan is back where it began, and saves where to start next time in $0394.

VIEW-WINDOW FIGURES, second half. The routine starts at $0FEF; this label sits on the page edge, inside the LDA #$01 at $0FFF, only so that the ledger's wall at $1000 leaves no part of the routine without an owner. From $100C it loops over objects and creatures 1-63, starting with the one saved in $0394 and wrapping from 63 to 1, and makes each one in the line of sight ($3EB0,x set) one of hardware sprites 1-7 of the top band. Its enable bit ($038A: 2, rolled left for each figure) is ORed into $038E. With d = player position - $CD - object position (16 bits in $038F/$0390; 128 map cells a row), X = $53 + 8 x (16 - (d AND $7F)) + $3FF0,x and Y = $C5 + 8 x (16 - (d >> 7)) + $4030,x, 8-bit, go to $3A02/$3A03 + 2n: that is X = 60 + 8dx + fine x (59 + 8dx from dx = +3 on, where the carry out of ADC #$53 stops reaching the next ADC) and Y = 86 + 8dy + fine y for a figure dx cells right of and dy cells below the player. Its colour, $A400 indexed by its glyph $4070,x, goes to $3A16 + n, and the glyph's 8 bytes in the character set ($3000 + 8 x glyph) are copied into the left byte of rows 0-7 of sprite block $3840 + 64n (pointers $E1-$E7). Stops after 7 figures or once round the list; the next start goes to $0394, so when more than 7 are in sight they take turns, and the enable mask, bit 0 (the player's dot) always on, goes to $3A10.
sprite 1's shape block, $3840 (pointer $E1); each next one 64 bytes on
in the line of sight? (flags set by $0FAA)
player position less $CD, then less the object's
no CLC follows: this carry goes into the next ADC
the figure's glyph
colour of that glyph
glyph bytes at $3000 + 8 x glyph
8 glyph bytes into the sprite's left column, 3 bytes apart
next object; 63 wraps to 1
enable mask into the top band's $D015 image

MENU CLEAR: blanks the menu area and empties the list of entries. Fills $03BF slots of $03BE characters from screen address $03C5/$03C6 ($05E0, text row 12) with spaces and the same cells of colour RAM ($D400 above the screen address) with 1, white; then points the next-entry address $0395/$0396 at the first slot and sets the entry count $0397 to 0. Either layout covers rows 12-15: 16 slots of 10 characters, four to a row (set by $3A79: the main menu and every submenu but one), or 8 slots of 20, two to a row ($3A93, the CAST menu). Called before each menu is built, and by the chooser $1320 on its way out.
colour RAM: $D400 above the screen address

MENU ADD ENTRY: adds one option to the menu being built. In: A = the value the chooser $1320 returns if it is picked (a verb number, an object or creature number, a spell number, or $FF for -NOTHING-), X/Y = address (low, high) of its zero-terminated PETSCII name. A is stored at $41C8 + the entry count $0397 first, even when the menu is already full ($0397 = $03BF): then it lands one past the slots and nothing is drawn. Otherwise the name is copied into the next slot ($0395/$0396) as screen codes: bytes $00-$1F (the $10 that starts each verb string) are skipped, and by the signed test so are $A0-$FF; $40-$7F lose $40; copying stops at the zero or after $03BE characters. Then the slot address moves on by $03BE and $0397 counts the entry.
stored before the full test
signed tests: $00-$1F and $A0-$FF are skipped
INC leaves the carry alone: this tests CMP #$20's carry

MAIN MENU: offers the options that fit the moment and returns the one chosen, 1-17 in A, numbered as the verb strings at $4130: 1 RUN, 2 PICK UP, 3 PUT DOWN, 4 INVENTORY, 5 OPEN, 6 CLOSE, 7 WEAR, 8 TAKE OFF, 9 PUT IN, 10 TAKE OUT, 11 LOOK IN, 12 ATTACK, 13 SWAP, 14 EXAMINE, 15 DRINK, 16 CAST, 17 UNCAST (0, WALK, is never offered). First redraws the picture strip ($149E empties it, $1695 shows what is in sight), counts the situation ($128F) and clears the menu ($1106); then adds with $1151, in this order: RUN always; PICK UP if an object lies on the player's cell; PUT DOWN and SWAP if either hand holds something; INVENTORY always; OPEN or CLOSE if the glyph under the player ($04CD, the centre of the view window) is a door, $F0-$FF: bit 0 clear (shut) gives OPEN, set gives CLOSE; WEAR if a wearable object is held; TAKE OFF if something is worn; if a container is carried, PUT IN (only with something in hand), TAKE OUT and LOOK IN; ATTACK if a creature shares the player's cell; EXAMINE always; DRINK if a potion is carried; CAST if no lasting spell is in force ($57D2 = $FF), else UNCAST (only MAGICAL SHIELD lasts, by $57D9, so while it is up nothing else can be cast). So a new game's menu is RUN INVENTORY EXAMINE CAST and options appear as the game goes on. Ends in the chooser $1320, whose result it returns.
glyph under the player: centre of the 11 x 11 view
signed test: $F0-$FF pass as doors, and so would $00-$6F
door bit 0: 0 shut (OPEN), 1 open (CLOSE)
lasting spell in force; $FF none

MAIN MENU CONDITIONS: counts what the main menu's options depend on. Zeroes $03A9-$03AE and $03BD. For objects 1-32: one at the player's map position ($3F70/$3FB0 equal to entry 0's) counts in $03A9 (PICK UP); one carried by the player (position 0: a position below $40 is the number of whoever holds it, so things in the backpack do not count) counts in $03AA if wearable ($4A81) and loose ($4AC1 = 0, in a hand: WEAR), in $03AB if a container ($4A41; among objects 1-32 only the backpack: PUT IN, TAKE OUT, LOOK IN), in $03AC if worn ($4AC1 = 2: TAKE OFF) and in $03BD if drinkable ($4B41, the potions: DRINK). $03AD counts the hands holding something ($4C01 right, $4C02 left; $FF is empty: PUT DOWN, SWAP, PUT IN). $03AE counts creatures 33-63 on the player's cell, dead or alive (ATTACK).
objects 1-32 on the player's cell
position 0: carried by the player
creatures 33-63 on the player's cell, alive or dead

MENU CHOOSER, used by the main menu and every submenu: the player picks a slot with the stick and fire, and its value from $41C8 comes back in A. The cursor starts on slot 0 ($0399 = 0; $9B/$9C = its screen address, from $03C5/$03C6), so the main menu opens on RUN. Waits for fire to be released, then loops: the cursor slot blinks, colour 0 (black) for 20 passes and 1 (white) for 10 (counter $03CE; $1483 does the colouring), each pass waiting $0F35 with A = 1 and reading the input through $179D. Stick right or left moves one slot (as far as index $03BF, back to 0), down or up one row, 40 characters and $03C0 slots (down while the index is below $03C1, up from $03C2 on); x is tested before y. A move onto a slot whose first character is a space is refused ($0398 keeps the old index); each accepted move waits $0F35 with A = $1E before the next. Fire, or the game ending ($03C7), leaves: waits $0F35 with A = 5 and for fire to be released, clears the menu ($1106) and returns $41C8 + slot. Nothing here advances the clock ($2C50 runs only in the step loop, at $08ED), which is why the clock stops while a menu is up.
wait for fire to be released
one pass of the blink loop
right: allowed up to index $03BF, one past the last slot
first character a space: an empty slot, refuse the move
auto-repeat delay after a move
chosen: wait for fire to be released
the chosen slot's value

MENU COLOUR SLOT: colours the menu slot whose screen address is in $9B/$9C by writing A to its $03BE colour-RAM bytes, $D400 above the screen address. The chooser uses 0, black, for the cursor and 1, white, to put a slot back. $9C is restored afterwards; X and Y are overwritten.

PICTURES CLEAR ALL: empties the picture strip at the bottom of the screen. Clears all 12 slots through $14C3 (bitmap blanked, slot freed, any DEAD sprite removed), marks objects 1-67 ($58C0-$5902: objects, creatures and the four feature pseudo-objects $40-$43) as having no picture ($FF) and zeroes the counts of door and staircase pictures shown ($59F9-$59FC). Called when a game starts ($0ABB), by the main menu before it redraws the strip, by WALK and RUN, and by the handlers that build object and creature submenus.
objects 1-67: no picture

PICTURE SLOT CLEAR: blanks picture slot X (0-11; X is kept). Its 4 character rows of 48 bitmap bytes, from $57E3/$57EF,x and $140 apart, are set to 0, the black background, so its colours need no clearing; $58B3,x = 0 marks it free. If a DEAD sprite sits on it ($59BD,x not $FF), that sprite's bit ($4960) is cleared from the bottom band's sprite enable mask $3A30 and both links, $59BD,x and $59C9 for the sprite, are set to $FF. A tall picture needs a call for each of its two slots.
a DEAD sprite on this slot?
4 character rows of 48 bitmap bytes to 0

PICTURE SHOW: puts object X's picture into the picture strip. In: X = object or creature (1-63, or $40-$43 for door and staircase pictures; X is kept), A = its tall flag ($586F,x). The strip has 12 slots in six columns at text columns 2, 8, 14, 20, 26 and 32, each an upper slot (even number, rows 17-20) over a lower one (odd, rows 21-24); $58B3 holds each slot's object, 0 = free. A short picture (6 x 4 cells) takes the first free slot, a tall one (6 x 8, $03CD = 8) the first free upper slot whose lower slot is free as well; with none free it returns and the object stays without a picture. Records $58B3 (both slots when tall) and $58BF,x = slot. READ INPUT, through the demonstration's player and recorder. Calls $0C94 (M toggles the music; joystick port 2 and the keys into $0387 fire, $0388 x, $0389 y), then acts on $03D3. 0, a normal game: returns. 2, the demonstration (set by the title code at $5BE9): real fire ends it ($03C7 = 1, $03D8 = 1, $03D3 = 0); otherwise the input is replaced from the recording through $03D4/$03D5 (bytes $A543-$A7FF, the random seed they need in $A540/$A541): each byte holds a code in its high nibble, played n + 1 times for the low nibble n; code bits 1 right, 2 left, 4 down, 8 up, $F fire, $E the end, which ends the demonstration as running into $A800 does. 1, recording (set by the title code at $5BCE, on $028D = 4 with key $11: probably CTRL+R): the real input is appended to the same buffer in the same form, a fire press as one $FA; F (key $15) writes the end mark $EF and ends the game ($03C7 = 1); a full buffer stops the recording. SWAP, menu option 13 (handler from the $4C03 table; its $4C27 entry makes the tick loop at $08CC run 3 ticks after it). Prints 'SWAP HANDS.' ($4868), starts a new message line ($28DD) and exchanges the object numbers in $4C01 (right hand) and $4C02 (left hand); $FF is an empty hand. Nothing is checked: two empty hands swap too, and the 3 ticks pass with the creatures moving. The right hand is the one ATTACK fights with ($2A73), so SWAP is how a weapon carried in the left hand is brought into use.

Once per game tick (from the tick loop at $0901): runs the passage check $20CC for every creature, entries $21-$3F, and then for the player, entry 0. Objects (entries 1-$20) are never moved this way. Dead creatures are checked as well; there is no body strength test.

Passage check for entry X: reads the map tile under its position ($3F70/$3FB0,x, through $9B/$9C). Tile $B1 adds $20 to the position, $B2 subtracts $20, $A3 adds $20. The map at $9000 is 128 cells wide in four 32-column sections, so $20 is the same row and column one section over. Only the cell changes; the fine position $3FF0/$4030 is kept. In the map each of the seven $B1 tiles lands on a $B3 with a $B2 beside it and each $B2 on a $B0 with a $B1 beside it: two-way links between neighbouring sections, probably stairs (the picture strip counts $B0 and $B3 tiles in view as features, $16DA, and the picture sheet holds a staircase). The one $A3, at $9718, drops one way into $9738. After a $B1 or $B2 move the $A3 test at $2101 compares the new position's low byte instead of the tile, so a landing with low byte $A3 would move a second time; no link in this map lands on one.
