Turns a displacement into a compass direction. In: $038A = dx, $038E = dy, sign-magnitude (bit 7 set = negative, magnitude 0-127; y grows southwards). Builds an index in $0392: bit 1 when dx >= 0, bit 2 when dy >= 0, bit 0 when |dy| > |dx| (the larger magnitude goes to $038F, the smaller to $0390), bit 3 when the larger is at least twice the smaller (the quotient is counted in $0393; a smaller of 0 is taken as a quotient of $20, straight). Returns A = $4947,index: 0 N, 1 NE, 2 E, 3 SE, 4 S, 5 SW, 6 W, 7 NW, so a target within about 26.6 degrees of an axis is approached straight and anything else diagonally; A = $FF when dx and dy are both 0.

Direction from one map cell to another. In: $038F/$0390 = the 'from' address and $0391/$0392 = the 'to' address (low/high). The column is the low 7 bits of the address and the row is the address shifted right 7 (the map is 128 bytes wide), so dx = to column - from column and dy = to row - from row, kept sign-magnitude in $038A and $038E; $2114 then returns A = 0-7 (N NE E SE S SW W NW) or $FF for the same cell. Overwrites $038A and $038E-$0393. Used by the chase ($2381), flee ($23AF) and go-home ($23D5) behaviours.

Creature clock, called six times per game tick by the tick loop at $08CC. Returns at once when the game is over ($03C7 non-zero), so the rest stop moving as soon as the player dies. For each creature Y = $21-$3F that is alive (body strength $4EC5,y not negative) it counts $4BC1,y up by one; when the count equals the creature's move period $4B81,y (3 for the minotaur and two hellhounds, up to 25 for the wizard; the table is never written) the count restarts at 0 and the creature takes one sub-step ($222E). So a creature gets 6/period sub-steps a tick; a cell costs it 9 of them, the decision and 8 moves, and every creature keeps moving whether or not the player can see it.

One sub-step, 1/8 of a cell, for creature Y. With no direction ($40B0,y = $FF) it decides one instead ($2308). Otherwise, if the creature makes footsteps ($59DC,y: orcs, wizard, skeletons, vampires, minotaur) and is in view ($3EB0,y), every third sub-step (countdown $5A1C,y) asks band 1 of the interrupt for a footstep noise ($03CF = 1). Then it moves by the direction's bits in $4957 (1 north, 2 south, 4 west, 8 east): the fine y $4030,x or fine x $3FF0,x runs 0-7 around the centre 4 and, when it wraps, the position $3F70/$3FB0 moves one row ($80) or one column. After 8 sub-steps ($40F0,x) the creature is at the centre of the next cell and the direction is dropped ($FF), so it decides again at its next sub-step. Direction 8, standing after an attack, has no bits: it only counts the 8 sub-steps.

Decision for creature Y at a cell centre. If it is in view ($3EB0,y) it re-arms its pursuit ($2367). If it stands on the player's cell and is not timid ($4D49,y bit 7 clear) it attacks ($23F9). Otherwise: with the flee flag $4CEC,y it counts the pursuit timer $4D2A,y down (the flag drops when the timer is already 0) and flees ($23AF); with the chase flag $4D0B,y the same countdown, then it chases ($2381); with neither it goes home ($23D5). The timer is reloaded at every decision made in view, so it counts decisions, about one per cell moved, since the creature lost sight of the player: 0 for the bats and one snake, 1 hellhounds, 6 orcs, 10 spiders, 20 skeletons, 30 vampires, 60 the wizard and the minotaur, 12 the timid snake.
bit 7 set: timid, never attacks

Arms creature Y's pursuit while it is in view: the timer $4D2A,y = its behaviour byte $4D49,y AND $7F, and bit 7 of the byte picks the mode: set = flee ($4CEC,y = 1; only the first snake, entry $3B, has it), clear = chase ($4D0B,y = 1). The other flag is left as it is; $4D49 is never written, so a creature only ever raises one of the two.

Chase: heads creature Y for $4C4F/$4C8F,y, where the player stood when it last had him in view (written by the sight check at $0FAA). Once on that cell it carries on in the direction it last moved (the opposite of its back direction $49B9,y, through $49F9): that is its search. The direction goes to $2566, which picks an open exit.
Flee: the direction from the player's last seen position $4C4F/$4C8F,y to creature Y, straight away from that cell, goes to $2566. A creature standing on that very cell goes home instead ($23D5).

Go home: heads creature Y for its lair $4CAE,y (low) / $4CCD,y (high); on the lair cell it returns with no direction, so it stands and decides again at every sub-step. But the new-game set-up at $0924 clears 64 bytes from $4CEC for the 31-entry flee flags and so zeroes every lair's high byte ($4CEE-$4D0C) and the low bytes of the last two ($4CEC, $4CED): in play every lair is in page 0, north of the whole map ($9000-$9FFF), and a creature going home heads north towards its starting column ($4CAE holds the start positions' low bytes) and never arrives. Seven wanderers ($22 $23 $2A $2B $2E $33 $35) are given a random map cell as lair every 50 ticks instead ($3B87).

Creature Y attacks the player (from $2310: it stands on his cell and is not timid). It then stands for 8 sub-steps (direction 8, count preset from $4FC3,y, which is 0 for every creature, $4FE4-$5002). Prints 'THE <name> ATTACKED YOU WITH ITS <weapon>.': the weapon is the highest-numbered object 1-$20 it carries (position $00yy) with the weapon flag $4B01 set, damage mask $4E45; without one, its natural weapon by type $4F66,y (HANDS, CLAWS, TEETH, STING, FIREBALL SPELL, names at $4FA6/$4FAC, masks $4FDE 1 3 3 3 15). To hit, (random 0-31) + skill $4E05,y, minus 8 while the magical shield is up ($57D3), adjusted by what the player carries ($24F1), must reach the player's defence $4DC7 (40; a signed compare): 'HE MISSED.' or 'HE HIT.'. Damage = (random AND the mask) + strength $4D89,y / 8, applied at $24CC. Returns Y = the creature.

Takes the damage in $038A from the player's body strength $4EC5 (entry 0 of the body array). This is the trainer's unlimited body strength patch point: its SBC $038A at $24D0 becomes NOP / SBC #$00. A negative result is death: 'YOU+RE DEAD...' ($48A9), $03C7 = 1 (the game-over flag the main loop tests; it then starts tune 1) and the M and B bars are redrawn ($2BDE). A body strength of exactly 0 is still alive.
trainer patch point: becomes NOP / SBC #$00

Adjusts a creature's to-hit roll in A for what the player carries. Each test wants the object's wearable flag $4A81,x to be 1 (it always is for these objects) and its position to be $0000, held by the player in a hand or worn, but not in the backpack: armour (object 1) -5, helmet (2) -2, ring $10 (the blue stone) +8, ring $11 ('PROTECTION FROM EVIL') -4. So armour or a helmet carried in a hand protects as well as when worn, and the blue-stone ring makes the player easier to hit. The shield test (-3 for objects $1E-$20 in the right hand $4C01 or the left $4C02) needs X to equal $1E, $1F and $20 at once, so it never subtracts: shields give no protection. Changes X.
never equal: X is $1E here
never equal: X is $1E here

Sets creature Y moving. In: A = preferred direction 0-7. Reads the tile under the creature and its exits from a 256-entry table (bit d = may leave in direction d): $A000 for a creature that opens doors ($5001,y = 1, patched in at $25A7), else $A100, where closed doors block. Tries the first six of the eight candidates listed at $4968/$4970 (d, d-1, d+1, d-2, d+2, d-3), skipping the way it came ($49B9,y); if none is open it turns back the way it came, unchecked. Stores the direction in $40B0,y, 0 in $40F0,y and the new back direction in $49B9,y. If it opened a door at its last decision ($4FE2,y) it now closes the door at its cell ($1C85); if the move leaves through a closed door ($A100 forbids it) it opens that door ($1BBF) and sets $4FE2,y. Returns Y = the creature.
operand high byte at $25A7 is patched: $A000 or $A100

High byte of the operand of LDA $A100,Y at $25A5: $2583 or $258B stores $A0 or $A1 here, so a creature that opens doors reads its exits from $A000 and the others from $A100. Both tables are loaded data (unchanged since the loader's hand-over), one byte per tile code, and differ only for the closed door tiles $F0, $F2 ... $FE. They lie in the part of the bitmap area that the bottom band never shows (with the vertical scroll of 3 in $D011, band 2 starts in bitmap row 16, $B400).
always the no-doors table: a closed door ahead?
no candidate open: go back the way it came

Installs the play-screen interrupt; called once, from the play set-up at $0A9D. With interrupts off it points the KERNAL's IRQ vector $0314/$0315 at $2653, clears the raster compare's high bit ($D011 bit 7), sets the first compare line to $28 (40), enables the VIC raster interrupt ($D01A bit 0), starts at band 0 ($03B7 = 0) and turns the music on ($03D1 = 1), then allows interrupts again.

The play-screen interrupt, entered from the KERNAL's IRQ entry through $0314, so A, X and Y are already on the stack. Writes the VIC's interrupt flags back to $D019 to acknowledge them; a raster interrupt goes on to the band dispatch ($2666), anything else (by its $DC0D read, a CIA 1 interrupt) leaves at once through $265D without the KERNAL. Three raster bands a frame, counted in $03B7: band 0 at line $28 (the text screen at the top), band 1 at $8E (the menu band and the sound), band 2 at $B6 (the picture strip, in bitmap mode).

Common exit of the play interrupt, for a non-raster interrupt and for bands 1 and 2: reads $DC0D, which acknowledges any CIA 1 interrupt, then pulls Y, X and A as the KERNAL's entry pushed them and returns (RTI). Only band 0 leaves through the KERNAL's handler ($EA31), so its keyboard scan and jiffy clock run once a frame.
Picks the band from $03B7: 0 = band 0 ($2675), 1 = band 1 ($275E), any other value = band 2 ($27AE).

Band 0, raster line $28 (40), above the text area: sets up the top of the screen (view window, message window, M and B bars and clock) and the menu band below it. Next interrupt at line $8E ($03B7 = 1). Reads $D01F and throws the value away, by its use to empty the sprite-background collision latch so that band 2 collects only the top band's collisions. $D018 = $1D (screen $0400, characters $3000), text mode ($D011 bit 5 cleared, and bit 7), VIC bank 0 ($DD02 and $DD00 bits 0-1 = %11), background yellow ($D021 = 7). Copies the top band's sprite registers from $3A00-$3A1C: positions to $D000-$D00F, then $D015 enable, $D017, $D01B priority, $D01C multicolour, $D01D, colours $D027-$D02E; then writes 0 to $D017, $D01D and $D010, so the copies of $3A11 and $3A14 never take effect and no top-band sprite is expanded or placed beyond x = 255. Leaves through the KERNAL's handler ($EA31).
read and discarded: empties the collision latch
undoes the $3A11 copy
undoes the $3A14 copy

Band 1, raster line $8E (142), the menu band: next interrupt at line $B6 ($03B7 = 2) and background colour 8 ($D021; the palette's orange, brown on screen). With the music on ($03D1, toggled by the M key at $0C94) it calls $1949, the tune's per-frame update ($C006). With it off, a footstep asked for in $03CF (by $0D44 as the player walks, or by $222E for a walking creature in view) is played once: the request is cleared and voice 1 gets volume 15 ($D418), frequency $1000, attack/decay $00, sustain/release $53 and the noise waveform with the gate set and cleared again two instructions later ($81 then $80). While the music plays a request stays pending. Leaves through $265D.
gate cleared again straight after being set

Band 2, raster line $B6 (182), the picture strip at the bottom; runs on to $2880. Next interrupt at line $28, band 0 of the next frame ($03B7 = 0). Counts the frame in $03A0 (waited on at $0914, $0ACA and $0AF1). ORs $D01F, the sprite-background collisions latched since band 0, into $038D: bit 0, the player's figure (sprite 0) touching foreground pixels of the view window's characters (by that use, a wall), is what makes the movement code at $0AD3 turn the player back. VIC bank 2 ($DD00 bits 0-1 = %01, $8000-$BFFF), bitmap mode on ($D011 bit 5), $D018 = $A8 (screen matrix $A800, bitmap $A000), background black. Sprites: positions from $3A20-$3A2F, enable $3A30, no priority or multicolour, all colour $0A (light red), x high bits $3A3D, all expanded both ways; all eight pointers ($ABF8-$ABFF, set to $94 at $0A76) show $A500, a sprite that reads DEAD. Leaves through $265D.
collisions since band 0

Adds up the weight of everything entity Y holds, into $03A2: for each object 1-$20 that is held ($3FB0,x = 0) by Y ($3F70,x = Y) it adds the object's weight $4A01,x and then calls itself with that object as Y, so the contents of a held container (the backpack) count too. X and Y come back unchanged. PICK UP calls it for the player (Y = 0) and for the object being picked up ($19F4, $19FA) and refuses at 70 or more ($1A03). A total past 255 would run into the BRK at $28AD; all 32 objects together weigh 131, so it cannot.
carry = the total passed 255

Trap for a weight total that carried past 255: BRK, which the KERNAL passes to its own warm start through $0316 ($FE66) with BASIC switched out. Unreachable in play: every object in the game together weighs 131.

Clears the message window: writes spaces over its $03B3 rows (8) of $03B2 columns (27), starting at the top-left screen address $03B0/$03B1 ($045C: row 2, column 12), leaves colour RAM alone, and puts the cursor column $03A3 back to 0. Called once, by the play-screen setup at $0AA0.

Starts a new line in the message window: moves rows 1-7 up one row, characters and colour RAM alike (27 columns from $03B0/$03B1, colour RAM = screen + $D400), fills the bottom row with spaces in colour 1 (white) and sets the cursor column $03A3 to 0. Called after most messages, directly or through $29F1. Uses $9B/$9C and $9D/$9E as the screen and colour RAM pointers.
Row loop: copy each character of the row below (Y + 40) and its colour up into this row, for the window's 27 columns.

Row done: both pointers one screen row (40) on; the INX INX / CPX $03B3 / DEX pattern stops once height - 1 rows have moved up (with a height of 1 it would only stop when X wrapped round, 256 rows later; the game always uses 8).
Blank the bottom row: spaces, colour 1 (white), then the cursor back to column 0.

Prints a zero-terminated PETSCII message (X = low byte, Y = high byte of its address) into the message window, a word at a time on the bottom row ($03B4/$03B5 = $0574) from the cursor column $03A3. Each word is measured first; if it would end past the last column (width $03B2 = 27) a new line is started ($28DD). Codes $40-$9F are shifted down by $40 to screen codes and every character gets the current colour $03A6 in colour RAM. A byte $01-$1F (or $A0-$FF) is a colour code: its low nibble becomes $03A6, so the $10 that starts every verb prints it in black. A space only moves the cursor on. The cursor column stays in $03A3, so consecutive calls continue one line. Uses $F9/$FA as the text pointer. A word longer than 27 characters would never fit and scroll for ever (the game's longest, at $52F7, has 15).

Next word: point $9B/$9C at the print line and $9D/$9E at its colour RAM, copy the cursor column to $03A4, and count the word's characters ($21-$A0) from the text pointer; a word of 255 characters makes it give up and return.
Word measured: $03A4 is now the column its last character would take. If that is not left of the width $03B2, start a new line first and measure again from column 0.
The word fits: print it from the cursor column, one character at a time, until a space, a colour code or the terminating zero.
A space: the cursor moves one column on, the text pointer moves past the word and the space, and the next word is measured.
The terminating zero: keep the cursor column in $03A3 for the next message and return.

A colour code: step the text pointer over it and make its low nibble the colour $03A6. The pointer moves one byte from the word's start, so a code in the middle of a word would print that word's earlier letters twice; the game's text has codes only at the start of a string or after a space.
Ends a sentence in the message window: prints "." (the string at $4943) with $2941, then starts a new line with $28DD. Called after nearly every message the game prints.

ATTACK, menu option 12 (handler table $4C03; the tick loop then runs 10 ticks, $4C27): prints "ATTACK ", clears the menu ($1106) and the picture strip ($149E) and offers every live creature ($21-$3F, body $4EC5 not negative) standing on the player's own square, plus -NOTHING-. The weapon is whatever the right hand $4C01 holds: an empty hand fights as FIST (object 0), anything that is not a weapon ($4B01,x = 0) refuses with "-NOTHING IN RIGHT HAND TO FIGHT WITH-". Prints "<creature> WITH <weapon>.", then rolls to hit and for damage (from $2AC9).
Creature loop, $21-$3F: listed when its map address ($3F70/$3FB0) is the player's and it is alive, with its noun ($4588/$45C9) and its picture ($586F,x through $1515).
A creature was chosen: keep it in $03A7, print its name and " WITH " ($47F9), then look at the right hand ($4C01) for the weapon.
Right hand empty ($4C01 = $FF): the weapon is the fist, object 0 (damage mask 1, $4E45).
Right hand holds something that is not a weapon: "-NOTHING IN RIGHT HAND TO FIGHT WITH-" on a line of its own, and no attack (the 10 ticks still pass).
Weapon in $03A8. A target already dead would get "IT IS ALREADY DEAD." ($4853); from this menu, which lists only live creatures, that cannot happen.
Print the weapon's name, FIST ($4827) for object 0 or its noun, and end the sentence.

To-hit roll: (random AND 31) + the player's skill $4E05 (25), + 8 while the Ring of Dexterity (object $12) is worn ($4AD3 = $4AC1+$12 = 2), passed through $2B5F for special weapons. A hit when the total minus the target's defence $4DC7,x has bit 7 clear; otherwise "YOU MISSED." ($482C, white).
+ player's attack skill (25)
state of object $12, the Ring of Dexterity: 2 = worn
target's defence

A hit: "YOU HIT." ($4839, blue), then the damage $038A = (random AND the weapon's mask $4E45,x) + the player's strength $4D89 / 8 (18 / 8 = 2): fist 2-3, dagger 2-5, sword, axe or mace 2-9. The Dagger of Death (object 6) against the minotaur ($3F) does 30 instead.
weapon's damage mask: 1 fist, 3 dagger, 7 sword/axe/mace
player's strength (18), /8 below
The wooden dagger (object 5, "IT IS MADE OF WOOD") against either vampire ($3D or $3E): damage 30.

Take the damage off the creature's body $4EC5,x. A borrow means it went below zero: its possessions fall to its square ($3B63) and "YOU KILLED IT." ($4843) is printed; the body is left at the wrapped, negative value.

Weapon-against-creature adjustments to the to-hit total in A (weapon $03A8, target X); returns the total in A. Of its three tests only the last can pass: (1) a mace ($16 or $17) against creatures $28-$2F would add 8, but the test needs the weapon to be $16 and $17 at once; (2) the wooden dagger (5) against the vampires would take $4E04 (60, vampire 1's defence), but needs X to be $3D and $3E at once; (3) the Dagger of Death (6) against the minotaur ($3F) replaces the total with $4E06 = $85, exactly the minotaur's defence, so that attack always hits.
never passes: A is $16 here, so it is never $17 (dead code to $2B77)
Second test, dead: the wooden dagger (5) against a vampire. The two CPX need X to be $3D and $3E at once, so $2B87-$2B8B never run.
never passes: X is $3D here, so it is never $3E
Third test, live: the Dagger of Death (6) against the minotaur ($3F) takes $4E06 ($85) as the total, equal to the minotaur's defence, so the hit is certain.
Pull the total, replaced or not, back into A and return.

Pseudo-random byte in A, read from the KERNAL ROM (banked in: $01 = $36 in play): A = ROM[$F000 + ROM[$E000 + i]] EOR ROM[$E800 + j], with i = $0383 and j = $0384; then i goes up by 1 and j down by 3. X and Y are kept ($0385/$0386). Since i + 1 and j - 3 leave (j + 3i) mod 256 unchanged, the output repeats every 256 calls; the title seeds i and j from $A540/$A541 ($F8/$18) whenever its scroller starts over ($5DF2), and every snapshot from the demonstration on is on that one 256-byte cycle. The three ROM pages it reads are identical in KERNAL revisions 901227-01, -02 and -03 (VICE's ROM files).
j - 3 (three DECs)

Prints a zero-terminated string (X = low byte, Y = high byte of its address) through the KERNAL's CHROUT ($FFD2), so its PETSCII control codes (clear screen, colours, cursor moves) work. Used for the play screen's frame at $50FA (the M and B labels, the empty bars, the 00:00;00 clock and the message window's border; from $0A3D) and, on the title, for the controls screen $838E and the instruction pages $84B7, $86E7, $8893, $8B1B and $8DB1 ($5C7C-$5CBE). Uses $9B/$9C as the pointer.

Draws the two strength bars on the top line: M for mind ($4F46) in cells $040D-$0414 and B for body ($4EC5) in $0417-$041E, in eighths of a cell: glyph $29 is a full cell, $22-$28 one to seven eighths, $21 an empty cell, and the cell after each bar ($0415, $041F) is written empty too. Mind shows 2 eighths per point (30 = 7 1/2 cells); body shows 2 x (body + 1) eighths, so a dead player (body negative) shows an empty bar. Called by the main loop every turn ($0824), the tick loop ($08E4), on the player's death ($24EA), after DRINK ($2E1F) and after a failed CAST ($2E7F). Values above 32 are never reached (the maxima are 30).
M bar: while 8 or more eighths remain draw a full cell; the remainder, 0-7, becomes the glyph $21 + remainder.
Full M cell ($29), move to the next cell and take 8 eighths off.
Fill the rest of the M bar with the empty glyph $21, up to and including the ninth cell $0415.
B bar from 2 x (body + 1) eighths; a body of -1 or less (dead), or 127 and more, was turned into 0 just before.
B bar: full cells while 8 or more eighths remain, then the partial glyph $21 + remainder.
Full B cell ($29), next cell, 8 eighths fewer.
Fill the rest of the B bar with $21, up to and including the ninth cell $041F.

The game clock, called once per game tick by the tick loop ($08ED), so it stands still while the menu waits. $03BC counts 8 ticks to a clock second (4 for the first one of a new game, $09F5). Each second it counts up the digit characters on the top line: seconds $0426/$0427 (00-59), minutes $0423/$0424 (00-59), hours $0420/$0421 (00-99); after 99:59;59 the display goes back to 00:00;00. How long a tick is in real time is not established: the tick loop waits for the frame only while walking or running ($0ABF).
A clock second: reload the divider with 8 and add one to the units of seconds ($0427).
Units of seconds passed 9: back to 0, carry into the tens of seconds ($0426, which go up to 5).
Tens of seconds passed 5: back to 0, carry into the units of minutes ($0424).
Units of minutes passed 9: back to 0, carry into the tens of minutes ($0423, up to 5).
Tens of minutes passed 5: back to 0, carry into the units of hours ($0421).
Units of hours passed 9: back to 0 and one more ten of hours ($0420); when that passes 9 it goes back to 0, so the clock wraps at 100 hours.

EXAMINE, menu option 14 (then 10 ticks): clears the menu and the picture strip and lists, with their pictures, the PEDESTAL (noun $40) when the player stands on its square $9677, everything the player holds (in a hand or worn: $3FB0 and $3F70 both 0; the backpack's contents are not listed) and everything on the player's square, dead creatures included; then -NOTHING-. For the choice it prints "EXAMINE <name>." and the description: $571E,x gives its number and $575F/$577B the address of its text (e.g. the pedestal's "A RAISED GOLDEN PLATFORM, THICKLY COVERED WITH DUST"). -NOTHING- prints nothing.
List entities 1-$3F: first the check for something the player holds, then for something on the player's square.
Not held by the player: listed when its map address ($3F70/$3FB0) is the player's.
Something chosen ($03A7): "EXAMINE <name>.", then its description through $571E,x (description number) and $575F/$577B (text address lows and highs), and the sentence ends.

DRINK, menu option 15 (then 10 ticks): lists the potions (objects with $4B41,x set: $0B-$0F) the player holds, not those in the backpack, prints "DRINK <name>." for the choice and uses it up. Effects by object number: $0B and $0F ("POTION OF HEALING") add 8-15 to the body $4EC5, up to the maximum $4E85; $0C (label "ALUMROF ECNEGILLETNI ARTXE", EXTRA INTELLIGENCE FORMULA backwards) adds 8-15 to the mind $4F46, up to $4F05; $0D ("IT SMELLS PUNGENT, THERE IS NO LABEL") halves the body; $0E ("POTION OF ORCANIAN INTELLECT") halves the mind. Then the hand that held it is emptied and the bars are redrawn ($2BDE).
A potion chosen ($03A7): "DRINK <name>.", then it leaves the game: $3FB0 = 0 (held) and holder $3F70 = $FF, which is no entity.
Healing, objects $0B and $0F: body + 8 + (random AND 7), no more than the maximum body $4E85.
Store the healed body strength.
Object $0C, the mind potion: mind + 8 + (random AND 7), no more than the maximum mind $4F05.
Store the restored mind.
Object $0D: the body strength is halved.
the crack's body trainer makes this $AD, LDA $4EC5
Object $0E, "POTION OF ORCANIAN INTELLECT": the mind is halved.
the crack's mind trainer makes this $AD, LDA $4F46
Empty whichever hand held the potion ($4C01 right, $4C02 left, $FF = empty), then redraw the M and B bars.

CAST, menu option 16 (then 20 ticks; the menu offers it only while no spell is sustained, $57D2 = $FF, $126B): shows the four spell names ($57CA/$57CE) and -NOTHING- in the two-column spell layout ($3A93, normal layout back with $3A79), prints "CAST <spell>" and compares the mind $4F46 with the cost $57D5,x (6, 10, 1, 5). Too little: the mind drops to 0 and "THE SPELL DID NOT WORK PROPERLY BECAUSE YOU DID NOT HAVE ENOUGH MIND POWER". Otherwise the cost is paid first, then: 0 MAGIC MISSILE at a creature in sight, damage 15, power 20; 3 ENERGY DRAIN at a creature in sight, damage 7, power 60; 1 FIREBALL on every creature in sight within two squares, damage 15, power 60; 2 MAGICAL SHIELD makes $57D3 = 8 and stays up ($57D2 = 2) until uncast. Damage goes through $3AC7.
Add the four spell names to the menu, with the values 0-3.
A spell chosen ($03A7): print "CAST " and its name, then test the mind against the cost $57D5,x with CMP / BPL (the sign of the difference).

Enough mind: pay the cost. The SBC has no SEC before it, but the CMP above left the carry set (mind at least the cost), so the subtraction is exact. A spell with an upkeep interval ($57D9,x not 0: only the shield) becomes the sustained spell $57D2, which swaps CAST for UNCAST in the menu.
the crack's mind trainer makes this NOP / SBC #$00
Magical shield (2): $57D3 = 8, which every monster's attack roll loses ($2491); end the sentence.
Magic missile (0): " AT ", a live creature in sight chosen with $3B17 (the mind is already paid, -NOTHING- wastes it), then $3AC7 with damage 15 and power 20.
Energy drain (3): " AT ", a live creature in sight chosen with $3B17, then $3AC7 with damage 7 and power 60.

Fireball (1): end the sentence, then $3AC7 with damage 15 and power 60 on every creature $21-$3F in sight ($3EB0,x) whose distance $5041,x is below 17 (8 per square): the player's own square, the eight round it and the four two squares away in a straight line. The player is not hurt.

UNCAST, menu option 17 (then 10 ticks; offered only while a spell is sustained), also called by $3A75 when the shield's upkeep finds no mind left: prints "UNCAST <spell>." for the spell in $57D2, clears the upkeep counters $03C3/$03C4, sets $57D2 to $FF (no spell) and, for the shield (2), sets the attack roll penalty $57D3 back to 0.

Character set of the top and menu bands, 256 glyphs of 8 bytes to $37FF: band 0 sets $D018 = $1D in VIC bank 0 (characters at $3000). Loaded with the game and never written (the same in entry-07f9.vsf). Screen codes are glyph numbers, and the map's bytes are glyph numbers too. Glyph $00, the '@' position, is a solid block; the groups that follow are labelled.
Glyphs $01-$1A: the letters A-Z at their screen-code places. The game's text is upper-case PETSCII, brought to these codes by subtracting $40 (the menus at $1151, the messages at $2941).
Glyphs $1B and $1C: an inverse M and B in a frame, the labels of the mind and body bars on the status line (PETSCII [ and \ in the screen frame string at $50FA).

Glyphs $1D-$1F: a 5, a 7 and a C crossed by a bar, in normal video. None of the game's own strings (messages $46B3-$4930, descriptions $51D1-$5704, the frame at $50FA) uses them; the title's text is shown in another character set.
Glyph $20: the space, blank; $1106, $28AE and $28DD clear the menu and message windows with it.

Glyphs $21-$29: the cells of the status bars, drawn inverted: $21 is solid (an empty cell, and the black status line and the solid row 11 below the windows); $22-$29 open 1 to 8 eighths of a channel three pixels high. $2BDE draws 8 cells a bar, so a bar holds 64 units.
Glyphs $2A-$2F: $2A blank; $2B an apostrophe at the '+' position (the game writes YOU+RE); $2C comma, $2D minus, $2E full stop, $2F slash.

Glyphs $30-$3A: the digits 0-9 and the colon drawn inverted, like the bar cells, so on the status line (colour 0 on the yellow background) the clock ($0420-$0427, advanced by $2C50) reads as yellow figures on black.
Glyphs $3B-$3F: $3B an inverted dot, the clock's separator between minutes and seconds ($0425, a ';' in the frame string); $3C a thin hook; $3D =, $3E >, $3F ?.

Glyphs $40-$4D: the message window's frame, printed by the frame string at $50FA: $40 top-left corner, $41 and $42 top edge, $43 top-right corner, $44 and $45 right edge, $46 bottom-right corner, $47 and $48 bottom edge, $49 and $4A the bottom-left corner, $4B-$4D left edge.
Glyph $4E blank; glyph $4F a 2 in normal video, which appears only in the map's last cells ($9FFD-$9FFE).
Glyphs $50-$53, multicolour map tiles in blue: $50 open water, $51-$53 water with a shore; they draw the small pool beside the pedestal ($95F5-$95F6) and larger ones in map rows 22-28.
Glyphs $54-$5F: blank (all zero).
Glyphs $60-$63, multicolour map tiles: $60 a small yellow mark under a wall line (three in map row 20; what it depicts is unknown), $61 and $63 floor with water at one side, $62 blank.
Glyphs $64-$6F: blank.
Glyphs $70-$73, multicolour map tiles: $70 a yellow block on the floor, the pedestal's tile at $9677 where putting down the amulet wins ($1B86); $71-$73 the water beside it ($9675-$9676).
Glyphs $74-$7D: blank.

Glyph $7E: solid rock, 1565 of the map's 4096 cells. Glyph $7F: solid too, the view window's 'not seen' cell that fills everything the rays have not reached ($0F45, $0DD6). Both have colour $08 in $A400, so they show black.

Glyphs $80-$B9: the dungeon's floor and wall tiles, multicolour. Floor is pixel pair %01 and walls are lines of pair %10 along a tile's edges ($91, the commonest, all floor; $81 a wall along the top; $83 top and bottom; $90 the left side); the curved cave pieces $8D-$8F, $9D, $9F and $AD-$AF fill their outer corners with %11 in black. The ray caster ($0C4F) stops at %10, so the walls block sight. The map never uses $93, $94, $9E (blank) or $A4.

Glyphs $B0-$B3: the ends of the passages. Whoever stands on $B1 (or on $A3) is moved 32 map columns right, on $B2 32 columns left ($20CC, for the creatures and the player); $B0 and $B3 are counted for the scenery pictures ($1710-$171E).
Glyphs $B4-$BF: $B4-$B7 more wall pieces, $B8 and $B9 black diagonal corners; $BA-$BF are not in the map ($BC a comb pattern, the rest blank).

Glyphs $C0-$CF: the items' small figures, shown as sprites in the view window ($4070 of each item): $C0 sword, $C1 dagger, $C2 axe, $C3 amulet, $C4 shield, $C5 mace, $C6 potion, $C7 ring, $C8 scroll, $CA backpack, $CB armour, $CC helmet. $C9 (a round bag) and $CE are figures no object uses; $CD and $CF are blank.

Glyphs $D0-$D9: the creatures' figures ($4070): $D0 orc, $D1 hellhound, $D2 vampire, $D4 snake, $D5 spider, $D6 bat, $D7 minotaur, $D8 wizard, $D9 skeleton; $D3, a figure with raised arms, is used by no object.
Glyphs $DA-$EF: blank.

Glyphs $F0-$FF: door tiles, multicolour. Bit 0 set = open; the door's other half lies below ($F0, $F4), above ($F2, $F6), right ($F8, $FC) or left ($FA, $FE), and OPEN and CLOSE change both halves ($1BBF, $1C85). The new-game setup closes every door ($09AE).

Shape of sprite 0 (pointer $E0 at $07F8) in the top band: the player's dot in the view window. The new-game setup clears $3800-$39FF ($0A45-$0A50) and writes rows 0-3 of its first byte column: $60, $F0, $F0, $60, a round dot four pixels wide; row 0 is $3800.
Sprite 0, row 1, first byte: $F0 ($0A59), the dot's second row.
Sprite 0, row 2, first byte: $F0 ($0A5E), the dot's third row.
Sprite 0, row 3, first byte: $60 ($0A63), the dot's last row; the rest of sprite 0, to $383F, stays zero.

Shapes of sprites 1-3 (pointers $E1-$E3), 64 bytes each from $3840: objects in the view window. The multiplexer $0FEF copies a visible object's glyph ($3000 + 8 x its $4070) into rows 0-7 of the first byte column ($10B4-$10CD, every third byte); the rest stays zero.
Shape of sprite 4 (pointer $E4), the fourth object slot of the view window; filled like sprites 1-3 and cleared with them at a new game ($0A4C clears $3900-$39FF).
Shapes of sprites 5-7 (pointers $E5-$E7), $3940-$39FF: the last three object slots of the view window, filled like sprites 1-4.

Sprite registers for band 0 (the top band), copied to the VIC each frame by the play interrupt ($26A2-$274D): $3A00-$3A0F go to $D000-$D00F. This byte is sprite 0's X, the player's dot: $3E + the player's pixel column $3FF0 ($0D27, $0D75, $1C72).
Band 0 image of $D001: the player's dot Y, $58 + the player's pixel row $4030 ($0D30, $0D96, $1C7B).
Band 0 image of $D002, sprite 1 X. The multiplexer writes sprites 1-7's X at $3A02 + 2 x slot ($105B): $53 + 8 x (16 - the column offset) + the object's pixel column, 8 bits (band 0 clears $D010).
Band 0 image of $D003, sprite 1 Y. The multiplexer writes sprites 1-7's Y at $3A03 + 2 x slot ($1082): $C5 + 8 x (16 - the row offset) + the object's pixel row.
Band 0 image of $D004: sprite 2 X, the second object slot, written by $105B.
Band 0 image of $D005: sprite 2 Y, the second object slot, written by $1082.
Band 0 image of $D006: sprite 3 X (third object slot).
Band 0 image of $D007: sprite 3 Y (third object slot).
Band 0 image of $D008: sprite 4 X (fourth object slot).

Upkeep of a sustained spell, called once per game tick by the tick loop ($08F0); nothing happens while $57D2 is $FF. Otherwise $03C3 counts ticks to 100 and $03C4 counts those hundreds up to the spell's interval $57D9,x (1 for the shield); each time both are full, one point comes off the mind $4F46. When the mind would drop below 0 it is held at 0 and the spell is uncast ($2F22). So the shield costs 1 mind point to cast and then 1 per 100 ticks (12.5 clock seconds).
the crack's mind trainer makes this $AD, LDA $4F46

Sets the menu band to its normal layout: 16 slots ($03BF) of 10 characters ($03BE), 4 to a row ($03C0); the stick moves down only from slots below 12 ($03C1) and up only from slot 4 on ($03C2). Called by the play setup ($09DF) and by CAST when the spell menu is done ($2E50).

Sets the menu band to the spell layout CAST uses: 8 slots of 20 characters, 2 to a row, down only from slots below 6, up only from slot 2 on; wide enough for spell names of up to 14 characters ("MAGICAL SHIELD"). $3A79 restores the normal layout.

Adds entity X (object or creature) to the current menu: its noun from $4588/$45C9 as the text and X as the value returned when it is chosen ($1151), and its picture to the strip in the bottom band ($1515 with its size flag $586F,x). X is kept. Used by EXAMINE, DRINK and the target menu $3B17.

A spell's effect on creature $03A7, with the damage in X and the power in $57D4: nothing if it is already dead. It hits when 31 + power minus its defence $4DC7,x has bit 7 clear. Both calls to the random routine ($3AD3, $3AE5) are wasted: the LDA #$1F at $3AD6 replaces the first byte and the second is never read. So a spell never misses what it can hit and never hits what it cannot: power 20 (magic missile) fails every time against vampire 1 (defence 60) and the minotaur ($85), power 60 only against the minotaur. The damage comes off the body $4EC5,x; if that borrows, the body becomes $FF, its possessions drop ($3B63) and "YOU KILLED THE <name>." is printed. A miss prints nothing.
Alive: the to-hit test, a fixed 31 + power against the creature's defence.
LDA, not AND: the random byte just fetched is thrown away
The spell hits: the damage comes off the body; a borrow means the creature is killed.

Target menu for MAGIC MISSILE and ENERGY DRAIN: clears the menu and the picture strip, lists every live creature ($21-$3F, body not negative) in sight ($3EB0,x, set by the view code at $0FCF) with its picture, and -NOTHING-. Prints the chosen creature's name, or "-NOTHING-", ends the sentence and returns the choice in X ($FF for -NOTHING-).
A creature chosen: print its name, end the sentence and return it in X.

A creature has died: every object (1-$20) it held ($3FB0 = 0 and holder $3F70 = X) is put down on the creature's square (its own $3F70/$3FB0) with its state $4AC1 set to 0 (loose), where the player can pick it up. Called by ATTACK ($2B51) and by the spells ($3AFC).

Called once per game tick by the tick loop ($08E1): every 50 ticks ($03C8 counts them) the seven wandering creatures get a new random destination from $3BBA: the orcs $22 and $23, the skeletons $2A and $2B, the hellhound $2E and the bats $33 and $35. The other creatures keep theirs.

Gives creature X a random destination, the map address it walks towards when it is neither chasing nor fleeing ($23D5): low byte $4CAE,x = a random byte, high byte $4CCD,x = $90 + (random AND 15), so anywhere in the map $9000-$9FFF, rock included. The two tables are indexed by the creature number, so their entries are at $4CCF-$4CED and $4CEE-$4D0C; the new-game setup at $0924 clears 64 bytes from $4CEC, which zeroes every creature's high byte, so only these seven wanderers ever head for a square inside the map.
Ray caster: 28 bytes, one per ray: the offset (7 x ray, $00-$BD) of the ray's 7-step pattern in $3BF7, read at $0B7C and again every 7 steps at $0C38.

Ray caster: 8 bytes indexed by the ray's pixel column $F7: 80 80 20 20 08 08 02 02, the high bit of the multicolour pixel pair under it. A tile's glyph row masked with $3BEF and equal to this, pair %10, stops the ray in any tile ($0C64).

Ray caster: 8 bytes indexed by $F7: C0 C0 30 30 0C 0C 03 03, both bits of the pixel pair under the ray ($0C57). In a tile whose $A400 colour is $0F (most door tiles, the pedestal's) a pair of %11 stops the ray too ($0C5F).

Ray caster: the rays' step patterns, 28 x 7 bytes to $3CBA; step codes 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, $FF stay (the ray moves by pixels, $0B8D-$0C1F). A ray repeats its pattern for 56 steps; the pauses keep every ray about 40 pixels, five tiles, long, so the view is round. This part: rays 0-6, from north (per 7 steps, ray 0 five up) turning towards east (ray 6 one up, five right).
Ray step patterns for rays 7-13 (see $3BF7): ray 7 due east (five right), turning south to ray 13 (five down, one right).
Ray step patterns for rays 14-20 (see $3BF7): ray 14 due south (five down), turning west to ray 20 (five left, one down).
Ray step patterns for rays 21-27 (see $3BF7): ray 21 due west (five left), turning north to ray 27 (five up, one left), which closes the fan next to ray 0.

69 bytes counting 0 to 68 ($3CBB-$3CFF). The view scroll uses the first 11, columns 0-10 of a screen row, with the same columns one row down from $3D00, to move the view window's rows up ($0E7E-$0E90) or down ($0EF0-$0F02) when the player enters the tile below or above; entries 64-67 serve at $3CFB.

Entries 64-68 of the counting table at $3CBB: $3CFB-$3CFE hold $40-$43, read at $1756 and $1772 as the object numbers whose pictures stand for the scenery counted in view ($59F5-$59F8: closed doors, open doors, tile $B0, tile $B3). $3CFF, 68, is not read here.
69 bytes counting $28 to $6C ($3D00-$3D44): column offsets of the next screen row (40-50 for the view's 11 columns). The view scroll reads $3D00-$3D0A with $3CBB; the entries after them are not read.

View arrays, one entry per view cell: 121 = 11 x 11 row by row, cell 60 the player's own tile. The rays fill them during a sweep ($0C77): this one the low byte of the cell's map address, $3DBE the high byte, $3E37 the tile. $7F in all three is a cell no ray reached ($0F45 refills them at every sweep). $0FAA matches the objects' places against these addresses. Runs to $3DBD.
View arrays: high byte of each view cell's map address ($90-$9F, or $7F not seen), 121 entries to $3E36 (see $3D45).

View arrays: the tile each view cell showed the rays, $7F if none reached it; 121 entries to $3EAF. At the end of a sweep $0F58 copies them to the view window at $0400 (11 x 11, colours from $A400), which is why the window shows only what is in the line of sight.

Per-object arrays, 64 entries each (0 the player, $01-$20 items, $21-$3F creatures), $3EB0-$412F. This one: 1 if the object's map address was among the view cells of the last sweep, else 0 ($0FAA, which also has each such object note where the player stood, $4C4F/$4C8F). Read by the view sprites ($100C), the pictures ($1697), a creature's reaction ($2308), its footsteps ($223D), the spell targets ($3B1F) and the fireball ($2EFD). Entry 0 is never set.

Each object's starting place, low byte (with $3F30), coded like $3F70: a map address, or the holder's number when $3F30 is 0 (the player starts at $947B; a scroll, $19, in the backpack; many items with a creature). Copied to $3F70 at every new game ($094C) and read nowhere else.
Each object's starting place, high byte: $90-$9F on the map, 0 when it starts held by another object; copied to $3FB0 at every new game ($0952).

Where each object is now, low byte (with $3FB0). With $3FB0 = $90-$9F, the low byte of its map address (128 tiles a row, 32 rows; the tile is the byte there). With $3FB0 = 0, the object holding it: 0 the player, 7 the backpack (the only container), $21-$3F a creature; $FF a drunk potion ($2DB3). Changed by moves ($0DA5-$0ECE, $2279-$22E8), the passage tiles ($20CC), the item verbs and a dying creature's drop ($3B63).
$3F70 entry of object 1, the armour. The monster-hit adjustment reads it with $3FB1 ($24F8): when the player has it, worn or not, 5 comes off a monster's roll to hit.
$3F70 entry of object 2, the helmet: read at $250C; when the player has it, 2 comes off a monster's roll.
$3F70 entry of object $10, a ring: read at $2520; when the player has it, 8 is added to a monster's roll, so monsters hit more often.
$3F70 entry of object $11, a ring: read at $2534; when the player has it, 4 comes off a monster's roll.
Where each object is now, high byte: $90-$9F, the high byte of its map address, or 0 when another object holds it (see $3F70). Carried by the player means both bytes 0.
$3FB0 entry of the armour, object 1, read at $24FD with $3F71.
$3FB0 entry of the helmet, object 2, read at $2511 with $3F72.
$3FB0 entry of ring $10, read at $2525 with $3F80.
$3FB0 entry of ring $11, read at $2539 with $3F81.

Each object's pixel column 0-7 inside its tile; 4, the middle, at a new game ($0979). The player's follows the joystick ($0D60, its dot at X = $3E + it) and wraps into the next tile left or right ($0DA0, $0DF6); a creature's follows its heading ($22B5-$22E2). Added into the object's sprite X ($1055).

Each object's pixel row 0-7 inside its tile; 4 at a new game ($097C). The player's follows the joystick ($0D82) and wraps into the tile above or below ($0E51, $0EC3); a creature's follows its heading ($2269-$229B); added into the sprite Y ($107C). $1C50, used by CLOSE, puts the player back to 4, 4 ($1C6A).

Each object's small figure, a glyph number: the multiplexer copies glyph $3000 + 8 x it into a view sprite and colours the sprite from $A400 ($1085-$1092). Items $C0-$CC, creatures $D0-$D9 (see $3600, $3680); the player's $7F is never drawn this way. Never written: loaded data.

A creature's heading: 0-7 = N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW (the step bits at $4957), 8 standing to fight ($2401), $FF choose again ($2302, after a tile's width of steps; every object at a new game, $095A). The step routine stores the heading it picks ($25D7). The player and items stay $FF.

A creature's pixel steps along its heading, +1 a step ($22F8); at 8 it chooses again. Zeroed when a heading is picked ($25DC); set to $4FC3 + creature when it stops to fight ($23FC), so it stands for 8 minus that. The player's and items' entries are never used.

The menu verbs, each a $10 byte (a colour code: black, when the message printer prints it) and a zero-terminated PETSCII word: WALK $4130, RUN $4136, PICK UP $413B, PUT DOWN $4145, INVENTORY $4150, OPEN $415B, CLOSE $4161, WEAR $4168, TAKE OFF $416F, PUT IN $417A, TAKE OUT $4182, LOOK IN $418D, ATTACK $4197, SWAP $41A0, EXAMINE $41A6, DRINK $41B0, CAST $41B8, UNCAST $41BF. Reached only through immediate operands (LDX #$36 / LDY #$41 for RUN): the menu builder $11A2 lists them and the handlers print them. Nothing prints WALK, so that option is never offered.

The value of each line of the menu window: $1151 stores A at $41C8 + line (the option number in the main menu, an object or spell number in a submenu, $FF for -NOTHING-) and $147F returns the chosen line's. With the 16-item window it can use 17 bytes, $41C8-$41D8, over the start of the loaded code after it that nothing calls (entry-07f9.vsf: 77 43 A9 01 2C A9 03 85).

Lines 8-16 of menu_line_values ($41C8): menu_add_entry ($1151) stores each line's value at $41C8 + line before it tests for a full window, so with the 16-line layout (menu_layout_normal) the stores reach $41D7, and $41D8 takes every entry a full list cannot show (the list's -NOTHING- included). Written only when a list is longer than 8 lines; as loaded the nine bytes are the start of the leftover monitor code that follows (STA $93 ends at $41D0, then LDA #$80, STA $020A, JSR $4DEE).

Leftover code, never run: 943 bytes ($41D9-$4587) of a machine-code monitor that was in memory when the game was saved and survives between the game's verb strings and its noun tables. Recognisable parts: a load/save/verify command that collects a quoted file name at $0230 (length $B7, device $BA) and calls KERNAL internals ($F3D5, $F5AF, $F68F, $ED09, $EE13...); a command dispatch on the letters T C F M H E D I A (from $4377); and an A command that packs a mnemonic with SBC #$3F and five rotates, as Supermon-style monitors do. Its JSRs and table reads land in the game's own tables ($4956, $4966, $49C2, $4A13, $4DEE, $4F59, $4F99...), so it cannot run in this layout, and nothing in the game refers to any address in it (absolute operands, immediate address pairs and every pointer table checked). Left untyped; recommended for exclusion from coverage.

Noun names, low bytes of the pointers: 65 entries ($4588-$45C8) indexed by entity number, 0 the player, 1-32 the objects, 33-63 the creatures, 64 the PEDESTAL; high bytes at noun_name_hi ($45C9). Every message or menu line that names a thing does LDA noun_name_lo,X / LDY noun_name_hi,X and calls print_message or menu_add_entry (35 reads of each: PICK UP, INVENTORY, PUT DOWN, WEAR, the attack reports, EXAMINE, DRINK, menu_add_entity...). One string serves every entity of a kind (four DAGGERs, five ORCs, seven BATs), so the player cannot tell them apart by name. Entry 0 points at 'N' ($460A); no read with X = 0 was found.

Entry 64 of noun_name_lo: the low byte of the PEDESTAL's name ($469A). verb_examine loads it directly (LDX $45C8 at $2CE8) when it adds entity $40 to the EXAMINE menu, which it does only while the player stands on map address $9677, beside the pool.
Noun names, high bytes of the pointers for entities 0-63 (64 follows at $4609): all $46, the strings lying at $460A-$46A2. Paired with noun_name_lo ($4588).
Entry 64 of noun_name_hi, the PEDESTAL's ($46), loaded directly by verb_examine (LDY $4609 at $2CEB).
The one-letter string 'N', where entry 0 (the player) of the noun tables points; no code found prints it.
Noun 'ARMOUR', entity 1 only.
Noun 'HELMET', entity 2 only.
Noun 'DAGGER', shared by entities 3-6: two plain daggers, 5 the dagger of wood and 6 the DAGGER OF DEATH, told apart only by their EXAMINE texts.
Noun 'BACKPACK', entity 7, the only container.
Noun 'SWORD', shared by entities 8 and 9.
Noun 'AXE', entity 10.
Noun 'POTION', shared by the five potions, entities 11-15; what each does depends only on its number (verb_drink).
Noun 'RING', shared by the five rings, entities 16-20.
Noun 'AMULET', entity 21: the Amulet of Immortality, which wins the game when put down on map address $9677 (verb_put_down).
Noun 'MACE', shared by entities 22 and 23.
Noun 'SCROLL', shared by the six scrolls, entities 24-29.
Noun 'SHIELD', shared by entities 30-32.
Noun 'ORC', shared by creatures 33-37.
Noun 'WIZARD', creature 38 (Leggoless, by the scroll text desc_wizard_heals).
Noun 'SKELETON', shared by creatures 39-44.
Noun 'HELLHOUND', shared by creatures 45-48.
Noun 'BAT', shared by creatures 49-55.
Noun 'SPIDER', shared by creatures 56-58.
Noun 'SNAKE', shared by creatures 59 and 60.
Noun 'VAMPIRE', shared by creatures 61 and 62.
Noun 'MINOTAUR', creature 63.
Noun 'PEDESTAL', entry 64: not an object but the fixed map cell $9677, named only in the EXAMINE menu.

'-NOTHING-': the cancel line every submenu ends with (menu_add_entry with A = $FF), and the word INVENTORY prints for an empty hand. Choosing it prints it only in ATTACK ($2A52), a spell's target menu (choose_creature_in_sight, $3B42) and PUT IN's container menu ($1EDE); the other submenus return silently.

Red: Thelric's parting words at the start of every game, printed by the new-game code at $0AA3: 'AS YOU LEAVE THELRIC SAYS...IF YOU DO NOT BRING ME THE AMULET OF IMMORTALITY AND PLACE IT ON THE PEDESTAL BY THIS POOL, YOU WILL NEVER RETURN HOME...'.
An empty string (only the terminator), printed straight after Thelric's words ($0AAA); print_message prints nothing for it.

' IN YOUR LEFT HAND, AND YOU ARE WEARING ' (INVENTORY, $1A8B), then the worn objects joined by msg_comma, or msg_only_clothes.

'NOTHING BUT YOUR CLOTHES': INVENTORY's ending when nothing is worn ($1AE2).

'POWER': unused, nothing refers to $493A (no immediate address pair, pointer or table entry).
', ' between the worn objects in INVENTORY ($1AB5) and between the contents in LOOK IN ($206D).
'.': print_full_stop ($29F1) prints it and starts a new line; it ends almost every report.

Compass direction for the class of a step (dx, dy) that direction_from_delta ($2114) builds in $0392 and reads back here ($2197): bit 0 set when |dy| > |dx|, bit 1 when dx >= 0, bit 2 when dy >= 0, bit 3 when the larger is at least twice the smaller (or the smaller is 0). 16 entries, values 0-7: 0 north (up the map: the address $80 lower), 1 north-east, 2 east, 3 south-east, 4 south, 5 south-west, 6 west, 7 north-west. A step within a factor of two of a diagonal gives the diagonal, otherwise the larger axis.

What each direction 0-8 does to a moving creature, one bit per unit step (creature_step, $225B, with the direction from $40B0): bit 0 up (fine y $4030 down, past 0 the map address - $80), bit 1 down, bit 2 left (fine x $3FF0 down, past 0 the address - 1), bit 3 right. 01 09 08 0A 02 06 04 05 for N NE E SE S SW W NW, and 00 for direction 8, the stand-still a creature is given when it strikes.

The eight single-bit masks 1, 2, 4 ... $80. creature_choose_move tests bit d of a tile's exit mask with it (can the creature leave that way in direction d); the picture strip uses it for sprite n's bit in the band-2 enable and X-MSB copies $3A30/$3A3D (picture_show, picture_slot_clear).
Low bytes of the eight rows of move_order, one per wanted direction 0-7; creature_choose_move ($258E) puts the row for its direction in $9D/$9E. Highs at move_order_hi.
High bytes of the move_order row pointers (all $49); lows at move_order_lo ($4968).

Order in which creature_choose_move tries directions when it wants to go north (0): 0 7 1 6 2 5 3 4, that is the wanted one, then alternately one step anticlockwise and one clockwise. Only the first six are tried ($2617 stops at 6), so 3 and 4 never are; a direction is passed over if it is the way back ($49B8) or the creature's tile has no exit that way. When none of the six will do, it turns back the way it came.
Try order when heading north-east (1): 1 0 2 7 3 6, then 4 5, never tried.
Try order when heading east (2): 2 1 3 0 4 7, then 5 6, never tried.
Try order when heading south-east (3): 3 2 4 1 5 0, then 6 7, never tried.
Try order when heading south (4): 4 3 5 2 6 1, then 7 0, never tried.
Try order when heading south-west (5): 5 4 6 3 7 2, then 0 1, never tried.
Try order when heading west (6): 6 5 7 4 0 3, then 1 2, never tried.
Try order when heading north-west (7): 7 6 0 5 1 4, then 2 3, never tried.

creature_choose_move's working byte: first the direction the creature must not take, its last step reversed (from creature_back_dir, $259D), then the reverse of the direction it chooses (from opposite_dir, $25BB), which it stores back into creature_back_dir ($25DF).

Per creature (index 33-63, live bytes $49DA-$49F8, zero at load): the reverse of its last step's direction, which creature_choose_move avoids next time unless nothing else is open. creature_chase ($23A0) turns it round again through opposite_dir to keep the creature going the same way once it has reached the place it last saw the player. Entries 0-32 are unused zeros.
The opposite of each direction 0-7: 4 5 6 7 0 1 2 3 (creature_choose_move $25BB and $261E, creature_chase $23A4).

Weight of each object 1-32, added up by sum_held_weight ($2890, which also counts what is inside a held container); PICK UP ($19EC) refuses with msg_too_heavy when the object, its contents and everything the player holds come to 70 or more. ARMOUR 40, HELMET 5, DAGGERs 3, BACKPACK 2, SWORDs 6, AXE 8, POTIONs 1, RINGs 0, AMULET 1, MACEs 8, SCROLLs 0, SHIELDs 10 (131 in all). The player (0) and the creatures (33-63) are given 100, which nothing reads.

Non-zero for a container: the BACKPACK (7), and entry 0, the player, which is never read (the objects he holds carry holder 0 in their position). main_menu_conditions ($12D2) counts held containers to offer PUT IN, TAKE OUT and LOOK IN; PUT IN ($1EA2) and LOOK IN ($1FDD) list them. Only 1-32 are read; the rest are 0.

Non-zero for an object that can be worn: ARMOUR, HELMET, BACKPACK, the five RINGs and the AMULET. WEAR ($1D0D, $1D2F) offers a hand's object only if it is set; main_menu_conditions ($12C5) offers WEAR when a held wearable object is not worn yet. player_protection also reads entries 1, 2, 16 and 17 (a_4A82 onwards) where a worn test might be expected. The byte here, entry 0, is 0.

Entry 1 of is_wearable, the ARMOUR's (1). player_protection reads it (LDX $4A82) together with the armour's position: whenever the armour is with the player, in a hand or worn, a creature's roll is 5 lower; the worn state in object_state is not tested.

Entry 2 of is_wearable, the HELMET's: with the player, held or worn, 2 off a creature's roll (player_protection, LDX $4A83). The bytes after it are entries 3-15, of which only the BACKPACK's (7) is set.

Entry 16 of is_wearable, RING 16's (the one with the translucent blue stone, by its EXAMINE text the sapphire the cursed-scroll text warns of): with the player, held or worn, a creature's roll is 8 higher (player_protection, LDX $4A91).

Entry 17 of is_wearable, RING 17's (-PROTECTION FROM EVIL-): with the player, held or worn, a creature's roll is 4 lower (player_protection, LDX $4A92). The bytes after it are entries 18-63: RINGs 18-20 and the AMULET set, the rest 0.

Where each object 1-32 is, beyond its holder: 0 loose (on the floor, in a hand or held by a creature), 1 inside the container whose number is in its $3F70 entry (PUT IN sets it, TAKE OUT and drop_possessions clear it, LOOK IN and TAKE OUT list these), 2 worn by the player (WEAR sets it, TAKE OFF clears it, main_menu_conditions counts it to offer TAKE OFF). The new-game set-up zeroes all 64 ($095F) and then sets entry 25 (state_scroll_25).
Entry 18 of object_state, RING 18's (-RING OF DEXTERITY-): the player's attack adds 8 to his roll while it is 2, worn (LDX $4AD3 at $2AD5). The bytes after it are entries 19-24.

Entry 25 of object_state, SCROLL 25's (-FORTES FORTUNA JUVAT-): the new-game set-up stores 1 here ($098B), so the scroll starts inside the BACKPACK (its starting position $0007 names holder 7). The bytes after it are entries 26-63.

Non-zero for a weapon: DAGGERs 3-6, SWORDs 8-9, the AXE (10) and MACEs 22-23. The player can ATTACK only with a weapon in the right hand ($2A7A; anything else gives msg_nothing_to_fight_with, an empty hand the FIST); a creature strikes with the highest-numbered weapon it holds (creature_attack_player, $2438), else with its natural weapon.

Non-zero for the five POTIONs (11-15): DRINK ($2D70) lists the held objects with it set and main_menu_conditions ($12E4) counts them to offer DRINK. What each does depends on its number (verb_drink, $2DB6): 11 and 15 add 8-15 body points up to body_start, 12 adds 8-15 mind points up to mind_start, 13 halves the body strength, 14 halves the mind power.

Per creature (33-63, live bytes $4BA2-$4BC0): how many calls of creatures_tick (six per game tick) pass between its actions, each a 1/8-cell step or a new decision (creatures_tick compares creature_tick with it, $221B). ORCs 6-9, WIZARD 25, SKELETONs 5-6, HELLHOUNDs 3-4, BATs 5-10, SPIDERs 4-6, SNAKEs 14, VAMPIREs 5, MINOTAUR 3; lower is faster. Entries 0-32 are leftover monitor code, never read.

Per creature (33-63, live bytes $4BE2-$4C00): counts creatures_tick calls up to creature_speed ($2212-$2218), then restarts at 0 as the creature acts. Zeroed for all 64 at a new game ($0962); a dead creature (body strength negative) stops counting.

The object in the player's right hand, $FF for none. ATTACK fights with it (the FIST when empty); PICK UP, TAKE OFF and TAKE OUT fill it first; WEAR, PUT IN, PUT DOWN, DRINK and SWAP take from it. player_protection's shield test at $2541 (CPX #$1E, then #$1F, then #$20, each followed by BNE) can never pass, so a SHIELD held here protects nothing.
The object in the player's left hand, $FF for none; it is filled when the right hand is full, and both full gives msg_no_free_hand. The same impossible shield test reads it at $2553.

Handler address for each main-menu option 0-17: WALK $08B0, RUN $08B9, PICK UP, PUT DOWN, INVENTORY, OPEN, CLOSE, WEAR, TAKE OFF, PUT IN, TAKE OUT, LOOK IN, ATTACK, SWAP, EXAMINE, DRINK, CAST, UNCAST. The main loop doubles the option through verb_offset and copies the entry into the operand of its JSR at $0846 (self-modifying: this byte read at $083A, the high byte at $0840). WALK is never offered by main_menu.
verb_handlers read one byte on (LDA $4C04,X at $0840) for each handler's high byte; the 35 bytes from here run from WALK's high byte to UNCAST's.

Game ticks each main-menu option takes: the main loop ($0830) copies it to $03AF before calling the handler, then runs the monsters, the clock and the spells ($08CC) for exactly that many ticks, even when the handler refused or -NOTHING- was chosen. The fire test at $0904 cannot end a timed action early: the input is polled in the tick loop only by the movement tick $0ABF, which runs only when $03AF is 0, and the menu returns after fire is released ($146C), so $0387 stays 0 (live: INVENTORY took its 12 ticks with fire held and without). WALK 0, RUN 0 (both last until fire is pressed), PICK UP 5, PUT DOWN 4, INVENTORY 12, OPEN 8, CLOSE 8, WEAR 10, TAKE OFF 10, PUT IN 5, TAKE OUT 5, LOOK IN 10, ATTACK 10, SWAP 3, EXAMINE 10, DRINK 10, CAST 20, UNCAST 10, and a 19th entry, 2, for an option 18 that does not exist.
Twice the option number (0, 2, 4 ... 40) for options 0-20, the main loop's index into verb_handlers ($0836). Only 0-17 have handlers; entries 18-20 would index past the table.

Low byte of the player's map address at the last sweep in which this entity was in his view window: view_find_visible ($0FD5) writes it for every entity 1-63 in view, and only creatures 33-63 are read, creature_chase ($238D) heading for that place and creature_flee ($23AF) away from it. As loaded, entries 0-32 are leftover monitor code (rewritten for objects that come into view, never read); entries 33-63 ($4C70-$4C8E) are 0.

High byte of last_seen_lo's map address (view_find_visible $0FDB; read at $2393 and $23B5). Like the creature arrays after it, its creature entries lie 33 bytes on, at last_seen_hi_creatures ($4CB0); the 31 bytes from here are its entries 0-30, leftover monitor code at load, rewritten for objects in view and never read.

Per creature (33-63, live bytes at creature_goal_lo_creatures, $4CCF): low byte of the map address it walks towards when it is neither chasing nor fleeing (creature_go_home, $23E1); random_destination ($3BBD) re-rolls it every 50 ticks for the seven wanderers (creatures 34, 35, 42, 43, 46, 51, 53). These creature arrays sit only 31 bytes apart, so each base's first bytes belong to the array before: the two here are last_seen_hi entries 31-32.
Entries 33-61 of last_seen_hi, the creatures' (62-63 follow at $4CCD-$4CCE, under creature_goal_hi's label); 0 at load.

Per creature (33-63, live bytes at creature_goal_hi_creatures, $4CEE): high byte of creature_goal_lo's map address (read by creature_go_home at $23E7, written only by random_destination at $3BC7, which gives $90-$9F). The two bytes here are last_seen_hi entries 62-63.
Entries 33-61 of creature_goal_lo: as loaded, each creature's own starting low byte (the same as its $3EF0 entry), until random_destination re-rolls a wanderer's; 62-63 follow at $4CEC-$4CED.

Per creature (33-63, live bytes at creature_fleeing_creatures, $4D0D): non-zero while it runs from where it last saw the player (creature_flee). creature_arm_pursuit sets it ($237D) when the player is in view and the creature's temper has bit 7 set; creature_decide clears it ($2342) when creature_mode_timer has run out. The two bytes here are creature_goal_lo entries 62-63 (VAMPIRE 62, MINOTAUR): 0 as loaded, and zeroed at every new game by the set-up's STA $4CEC,Y for Y = 0-63 ($0965), which also runs over all of creature_goal_hi's creature entries.

Entries 33-61 of creature_goal_hi: 0 as loaded and zeroed again at every new game (the set-up's STA $4CEC,Y runs over them), so only the seven wanderers ever get a real page. With a high byte of 0 direction_towards gets a target row of 0 or 1, above every map row, so an idle creature that does not wander always heads north, towards its starting column, rather than round a lair.

Per creature (33-63, live bytes at creature_chasing_creatures, $4D2C): non-zero while it heads for where it last saw the player (creature_chase). creature_arm_pursuit sets it ($2377) when the player is in view and the creature's temper has bit 7 clear; creature_decide clears it ($2358) when creature_mode_timer has run out. The two bytes here are creature_goal_hi entries 62-63.
Entries 33-61 of creature_fleeing (62-63 at $4D2A-$4D2B); 0 at load and zeroed at every new game ($0965).

Per creature (33-63, live bytes at creature_mode_timer_creatures, $4D4B): moves left in its chase or flight. creature_arm_pursuit reloads it with temper bits 0-6 ($236C) at every decision made while the player is in view; creature_decide counts it down ($234B for a flight, $2361 for a chase) and ends the mode when it is 0. The two bytes here are creature_fleeing entries 62-63.
Entries 33-61 of creature_chasing (62-63 at $4D49-$4D4A); 0 at load and zeroed at every new game ($0968).

Per creature (33-63, values at creature_temper_creatures, $4D6A): bit 7 set = it flees when it sees the player and never attacks (creature_decide tests it at $2320); bits 0-6 = how many moves its chase or flight lasts after the player was last in view (creature_arm_pursuit, $2367-$236F). The two bytes here are creature_chasing entries 62-63.
Entries 33-63 of creature_mode_timer; 0 at load.

Entries 33-63 of creature_temper: ORCs 6, WIZARD 60, SKELETONs 20, HELLHOUNDs 1, BATs 0 (they follow only while they see the player), SPIDERs 10, SNAKE 59 $8C (flees for 12 moves and never attacks, the only timid creature), SNAKE 60 0, VAMPIREs 30, MINOTAUR 60.

Strength of the player (entry 0, 18, read at $2B0B) and each creature (33-63, read at $24BF): a hit does the weapon's damage plus strength / 8. ORCs 10-18, WIZARD 30, SKELETONs 15-19, HELLHOUNDs 5, BATs 2, SPIDERs 10, SNAKEs 3, VAMPIRE 61 40. The next table, defence, starts only $3E on, so VAMPIRE 62's strength and the MINOTAUR's are defence's first two bytes ($4DC7-$4DC8: 40 and 21). Entries 1-32 are leftover monitor code.

What an attacker's roll must reach to hit (CMP then BPL, a hit when the difference has bit 7 clear): the player's (entry 0, 40, at $2497) and each creature's (33-63: at $2AE5 for the player's blows, $3ADF for spells). ORCs 20-30, WIZARD 40, SKELETONs 15-25, HELLHOUNDs 15-20, BATs 10-15, SPIDERs 35, SNAKEs 50; VAMPIRE 61's is defence_vampire61 ($4E04); VAMPIRE 62's and the MINOTAUR's are the first two bytes of to_hit ($4E05-$4E06). Entries 0-1 double as strength 62-63; 2-32 are leftover monitor code.

Entry 61 of defence, VAMPIRE 61's: 60, which the player's roll (25 + 0-31) reaches only with the RING OF DEXTERITY worn. attack_special_roll would load it as the roll for the DAGGER OF WOOD against a VAMPIRE (LDA $4E04 at $2B88), but its test (CPX #$3D, BNE, CPX #$3E, BNE) can never pass.

Added to an attacker's random 0-31 to make its roll: the player's (entry 0, 25, at $2AD2) and each creature's (33-63, at $248D). This byte is also entry 62 of defence, so VAMPIRE 62's defence is the player's 25. The creatures' values follow in to_hit_1's bytes.

Entry 1 of to_hit (an object's, unused) and entry 63 of defence: the MINOTAUR's defence, $85 (133), which no roll reaches, except that attack_special_roll (LDA $4E06 at $2B98) makes it the roll itself when the player strikes the MINOTAUR with the DAGGER OF DEATH (object 6), so that blow always hits. The bytes after it are to_hit entries 2-63: 2-32 leftover monitor code, then ORCs 15-25, WIZARD 20, SKELETONs 15-28, HELLHOUNDs 22-25, BATs 18-21, SPIDERs 30-35, SNAKEs 20, VAMPIREs 36 and 38, MINOTAUR 45.

Damage mask of each weapon, by object number, with entry 0 the FIST: a hit does (random AND mask) + the attacker's strength / 8. FIST 1, DAGGERs 3, SWORDs, AXE and MACEs 7, every other object 0. Read at $2B05 for the player (X = weapon, 0 for the fist) and $245D for a creature's weapon. The player's blow does 30 instead with the DAGGER OF DEATH (6) on the MINOTAUR and the DAGGER OF WOOD (5) on a VAMPIRE ($2B18-$2B3F). Entries 33-63 are 0.

Starting and largest body strength: copied into body_strength at every new game ($096B); the player's (30) is also the ceiling for the healing potions ($2DC9). ORCs 12-15, WIZARD 20, SKELETONs 20, HELLHOUNDs 10-15, BATs 1-6, SPIDERs 10-15, SNAKEs 20, VAMPIREs 50, MINOTAUR 50. Entries 1-32 are leftover monitor code (objects have no body strength).

Current body strength: entry 0 the player's (the B bar), 33-63 the creatures'; bit 7 set = dead. A creature's blow subtracts at player_body_hit ($24D0, the trainer's body patch point) and the game ends when it goes negative (msg_youre_dead); the player's blows subtract at $2B49 (a wrapped negative result = killed) and a spell kill stores $FF ($3AF9). Potions 11 and 15 add 8-15 up to body_start, potion 13 halves it ($2DF8). Filled for all 64 from body_start at a new game; entries 1-32 are copies of leftover bytes, never read.

Starting and largest mind power: copied into mind_power at every new game ($0971) and the ceiling for potion 12 ($2DE6). Only entry 0, the player's 30, means anything: entries 1-63 ($4F06-$4F44) are leftover monitor data, a 6502 disassembler's addressing-mode table (the Apple II monitor's format table in nibble-swapped form), and the byte after them, $4F45, is part of the same leftover.

Current mind power; only entry 0, the player's, is used: the M bar (draw_mind_body_bars), spell costs (verb_cast, $2E93; too little sets it to 0 at $2E7C), the shield's upkeep (spell_upkeep, $3A66), potion 12 adding 8-15 up to mind_start and potion 14 halving it ($2E02). The new-game loop fills all 64 from mind_start, $41 bytes back (not $40); entries 1-63 are never read. Its entries 32-63 lie under natural_weapon's label.

Per creature (33-63, values at natural_weapon_creatures, $4F87): what it fights with when it holds no weapon, an index 0-5 into natural_weapon_name_lo/hi and natural_weapon_damage (creature_attack_player, $2466 and $247A). The 33 bytes from here to $4F86 are mind_power entries 32-63 and one unused byte.

Entries 33-63 of natural_weapon: ORCs, SKELETONs and the MINOTAUR 1 (HANDS); the WIZARD 5 (FIREBALL SPELL); HELLHOUNDs, BATs and VAMPIREs 3 (TEETH); SPIDERs and SNAKEs 4 (STING). 0 (NULL) and 2 (CLAWS) are never used.

Low bytes of the six natural weapons' names (NULL, HANDS, CLAWS, TEETH, STING, FIREBALL SPELL), printed after msg_attacked_you_with_its when the attacker holds no weapon ($246D); highs at natural_weapon_name_hi.
High bytes of the six natural weapon name pointers (all $4F); lows at natural_weapon_name_lo ($4FA6).
Natural weapon 0, 'NULL' (damage mask 0): no creature has it.
Natural weapon 1, 'HANDS' (damage mask 1): the ORCs', SKELETONs' and MINOTAUR's.
Natural weapon 2, 'CLAWS' (damage mask 3): no creature has it.

Natural weapon 3, 'TEETH' (damage mask 3): the HELLHOUNDs', BATs' and VAMPIREs'. creature_attack_player also reads this address as a per-creature table (LDA $4FC3,Y at $23F9, the step count put in $40F0 when a creature strikes); its creature entries are attack_pause_creatures ($4FE4-$5002).
Natural weapon 4, 'STING' (damage mask 3): the SPIDERs' and SNAKEs'.
Natural weapon 5, 'FIREBALL SPELL' (damage mask 15, the largest of any attack): the WIZARD's, so the scroll's 'KIND OLD WIZARD' attacks with fireballs.
Damage mask of each natural weapon (a hit does random AND mask + strength / 8; creature_attack_player $247E): NULL 0, HANDS 1, CLAWS 3, TEETH 3; STING 3 and FIREBALL SPELL 15 follow at $4FE2-$4FE3.

Per creature (33-63, live bytes at closes_door_creatures, $5003): set when a move of its went through a shut door, which creature_choose_move opened (door_open, $2600; flag set at $260A); at its next move creature_choose_move clears the flag ($25EF) and closes the door at the creature's cell (door_close, $25F4). The two bytes here are natural_weapon_damage entries 4-5: STING 3, FIREBALL SPELL 15.

Entries 33-61 of the per-creature table creature_attack_player reads at $4FC3,Y (62-63 at $5001-$5002): the step count a creature's move counter $40F0 restarts from when it strikes, with direction 8 (stand), so 8 minus it steps pass before its next decision. All 0: every creature waits the full 8 steps.

Per creature (33-63, live bytes at opens_doors_creatures, $5022): non-zero if it can open doors. creature_choose_move ($257C) then patches exits_table_page to take its exits from tile_exits_door_opener ($A000, shut doors passable) instead of tile_exits ($A100), and opens a door it steps through. The two bytes here are the attack pause entries 62-63, both 0.
Entries 33-63 of creature_closes_door; 0 at load.
Entries 33-63 of creature_opens_doors: 1 for the ORCs, the WIZARD, the SKELETONs, the VAMPIREs and the MINOTAUR; 0 for the HELLHOUNDs, BATs, SPIDERs and SNAKEs.

How far each entity (1-63) is from the player: view_distance's value for the view cell it stands on (8 per cell, 1 on the player's own cell), 0 when it is not in view; view_find_visible clears 1-63 ($0FB1) and refills it ($0FE1) at every sweep. FIREBALL (verb_cast, $2F02) burns the creatures in sight with a value below 17: the player's cell, the eight around it and the four two cells away in a straight line. Entry 0 is not used.

Distance from the centre of the 11 x 11 view window for each of its 121 cells, row by row (cell n is at row n / 11, column n mod 11, as the cell list at $3D45/$3DBE): about 8 x the distance in cells, rounded (a few cells a unit off), with the centre 1 so that 0 can mean out of view; 8 beside the player, 12 diagonally, 40 at the middle of an edge, 57 in a corner. view_find_visible ($0FDE) copies a visible entity's value into distance_from_player. This label covers rows 0-4, the cells above the player.
Rows 5-10 of view_distance: the player's own row (the centre cell, value 1, is $50BD) and the five rows below it.

The play screen's fixed frame, printed once through the KERNAL's CHROUT by print_via_chrout ($0A39) as a game starts: clear screen and black, then row 0 with the M and B labels ('[' and '\', screen codes $1B and $1C, an inverse M and B in this character set), solid blocks where the two bars go and '00:00;00' for the clock (hours:minutes;seconds, redrawn by draw_mind_body_bars and advance_clock); rows 1-10 the message window's border (PETSCII $60-$6D, screen codes $40-$4D: corners, edges and their decorated variants), placed with cursor-down, cursor-left and HOME; row 11 forty solid blocks ('!', screen code $21, a full cell in this character set).
EXAMINE text 0 (red, like all 28): 'NO DISTINGUISHING FEATURES', for DAGGERs 3-4, the SWORDs, the AXE, RINGs 19-20 and every BAT, SPIDER, SNAKE and VAMPIRE.
EXAMINE text 1: 'THERE IS A LABEL ON IT WHICH SAYS -POTION OF HEALING-', for POTIONs 11 and 15; true, verb_drink gives them 8-15 body points.
EXAMINE text 2: 'IT IS QUITE LARGE AND HAS SHOULDER STRAPS', for the BACKPACK (7).

EXAMINE text 3: 'THE WRITING ON IT SAYS -THE SAPPHIRE IS CURSED, IT BRINGS BAD LUCK-'. Never shown: no entry of description_of is 3. The warning fits RING 16 (the blue stone), which does make creatures' rolls 8 higher while the player has it (player_protection).
EXAMINE text 4: 'IT HAS A LARGE TRANSLUCENT BLUE STONE FIXED TO IT', for RING 16, the cursed one.
EXAMINE text 5: 'IT HAS A SHARP EDGE AND A LONG BLADE'. Never shown: no entry of description_of is 5 (by its words a sword's; the SWORDs show text 0).
EXAMINE text 6: 'THE LABEL READS...ALUMROF ECNEGILLETNI ARTXE' ('EXTRA INTELLIGENCE FORMULA' backwards), for POTION 12, which adds 8-15 mind points.
EXAMINE text 7: 'IT SMELLS PUNGENT, THERE IS NO LABEL', for POTION 13, which halves the body strength.
EXAMINE text 8: 'POTION OF ORCANIAN INTELLECT', for POTION 14, which halves the mind power.
EXAMINE text 9: 'FIND PROTECTION FOR YOUR HEALTH, GATHER POTIONS FOR YOUR STEALTH, GO UP AND EAST TO FIND YOUR TREASURE, BEWARE THE MINOTAUR OR BE HIS PLEASURE', for SCROLL 24.

EXAMINE text 11: 'THE KIND OLD WIZARD LEGGOLESS WILL HEAL YOUR WOUNDS', for SCROLL 27. No healing by the WIZARD was found: he chases the player for 60 moves and strikes with a FIREBALL SPELL (natural weapon 5); only POTIONs 11 and 15 raise the player's body strength.
EXAMINE text 12: 'A MYSTICAL GLOW SURROUNDS THIS VALUABLE TREASURE', for the AMULET (21).

EXAMINE text 13: 'IT IS HEAVY AND WILL PROVIDE GOOD PROTECTION IF WORN', for the ARMOUR and the HELMET; they take 5 and 2 off a creature's roll whenever the player has them, worn or not (player_protection).
EXAMINE text 14: 'THE WORDS -DAGGER OF DEATH- ARE INSCRIBED ON THE BLADE', for DAGGER 6.
EXAMINE text 15: '-PROTECTION FROM EVIL- IS INSCRIBED ON IT', for RING 17 (4 off a creature's roll).
EXAMINE text 16: '-RING OF DEXTERITY- IS INSCRIBED ON IT', for RING 18 (8 on the player's roll while worn).
EXAMINE text 17: 'A STRONG LEATHER HAND HELD SHIELD', for SHIELDs 30-32; held, a shield protects nothing, player_protection's shield test being unpassable.
EXAMINE text 18: 'IT IS MADE OF WOOD', for DAGGER 5, the dagger of wood.
EXAMINE text 19: 'IT READS -AS SURELY AS THE EAST WIND BLOWS, THE DAGGER OF WOOD IS THE VAMPIRES FOE-', for SCROLL 28; the DAGGER OF WOOD does 30 to a VAMPIRE ($2B2B-$2B3F).
EXAMINE text 20: 'IT READS -FORTES FORTUNA JUVAT-' (fortune favours the brave), for SCROLL 25, which starts inside the BACKPACK.
EXAMINE text 21: 'A LARGE DIM-WITTED CAVE DWELLER', for the ORCs (33-37).
EXAMINE text 22: 'A SHORT HARMLESS LOOKING WIZARD', for the WIZARD (38), who attacks with a FIREBALL SPELL.
EXAMINE text 23: 'A CHAOTIC UNDEAD CREATURE', for the SKELETONs (39-44).
EXAMINE text 24: 'IT IS A FIERCE SABRE TOOTHED WOLF', for the HELLHOUNDs (45-48).
EXAMINE text 25: 'IT IS AN ENORMOUS GRUESOME LOOKING HALF BULL, HALF MAN', for the MINOTAUR (63).
EXAMINE text 26: 'GOOD FOR CRUSHING BONES', for the MACEs (22-23); the extra 8 against skeletons that attack_special_roll seems meant to give never comes (its test at $2B63 cannot pass).
EXAMINE text 27: 'A RAISED GOLDEN PLATFORM, THICKLY COVERED WITH DUST', for the PEDESTAL (64).

EXAMINE text number (0-27) of each entity 0-63: verb_examine ($2D4C) looks it up and prints the text at desc_ptr_lo/hi. Kinds share texts, and text 0 'NO DISTINGUISHING FEATURES' serves the plain DAGGERs, the SWORDs, the AXE, RINGs 19-20 and every BAT, SPIDER, SNAKE and VAMPIRE. Texts 3 (the cursed-sapphire warning) and 5 (the long blade) are chosen by no entity, so they are never shown. Entry 64, the PEDESTAL's, follows at $575E.
Entry 64 of description_of: 27, the PEDESTAL's text (desc_pedestal).
Low bytes of the 28 EXAMINE texts' addresses ($51D0-$56EA), indexed by description_of's number (verb_examine, $2D50); highs at desc_ptr_hi.
High bytes of the 28 EXAMINE text addresses ($51-$56; verb_examine, $2D53); lows at desc_ptr_lo ($575F).
Spell 0, 'MAGIC MISSILE' (cost 6): 15 body points off one creature in sight, spell power 20 (spell_hit_creature).
Spell 1, 'FIREBALL' (cost 10): 15 off every creature in sight with distance_from_player below 17, power 60.
Spell 2, 'MAGICAL SHIELD' (cost 1, then 1 mind point per 100 ticks): 8 off every creature's attack roll (shield_protection) until it is uncast or the mind runs out.
Spell 3, 'ENERGY DRAIN' (cost 5): 7 body points off one creature in sight, power 60.
Low bytes of the four spell names (CAST's menu $2E2D, its report $2E65, UNCAST's report $2F2C); highs at spell_name_hi.
